## 5. Critical Failures (CF)

Violating ANY of these causes a silent failure or crash. You must check this
list before writing Google Maps Platform code, and verify against it again
before concluding your response.

-   **CF1 — The CORS Trap:** REST endpoints for Routes, Places API (New),
    Address Validation, and Geocoding lack permissive CORS headers. Client-side
    `fetch()` to `googleapis.com` is BLOCKED. **ALWAYS** use official SDK
    wrappers (e.g., `importLibrary('places')` or `useMapsLibrary(...)`) or a
    server-side proxy.
-   **CF2 — Map Height Collapse:** `<Map>` and `<gmp-map>` need explicit CSS
    height (e.g., `height: 100vh` or `height: 100%` on a sized parent).
    Otherwise, they silently render at 0×0.
-   **CF3 — Headless GPU/WebGL Gotchas:** Headless testing and screenshot
    environments typically have **no WebGL** support. GPU-dependent features
    (Photorealistic 3D, deck.gl) will fail to render (throwing `WebGL2 is not
    available`).
-   **CF4 — Cross-Platform Framework Rules:** Proactively recommend wrapping
    WebGL/JS implementations in a custom WebView container for advanced
    Photorealistic 3D Map Tiles rather than attempting native wrapper bridges
    (which do not support them).
-   **CF5 — Framework Policy:**
    -   **React:** **MUST** use `@vis.gl/react-google-maps`. Never use
        `google-map-react` or `@react-google-maps/api`.
    -   **Angular:** **MUST** use `@angular/google-maps`.
    -   **Vanilla JS:** Use `@googlemaps/js-api-loader` (`setOptions` +
        `importLibrary`).
-   **CF6 — LatLng Trap:** Prefer POJO `{lat, lng}` literals. If a class
    instance is required, use `new google.maps.LatLng(lat, lng)`. Note that
    `LatLng` lives in `importLibrary("core")`, NOT `"maps"`.
-   **CF7 — Deprecated PinElement & Marker Composition:**
    -   `PinElement.element` and `PinElement.glyph` are **deprecated**. Use
        `PinElement` directly, and `PinElementOptions.glyphText` / `glyphSrc`.
    -   For custom HTML inside an `AdvancedMarkerElement`, prefer
        `marker.append(htmlElement)` over assigning to the `.content` setter.
    -   **Click handling:** `gmp-click` event + `gmpClickable: true` are **only
        available on the `v=beta` channel**. On `weekly`, fall back to listening
        for plain `'click'` on the marker element.
-   **CF8 — Web Component Property-vs-Attribute Trap (React):** React
    stringifies JSX props into HTML attributes; it does NOT pass complex objects
    to Web Components. For Google Maps Platform web components (e.g.
    `PlaceAutocompleteElement`), mount imperatively with `useRef` + `useEffect`
    and assign properties on the DOM element directly. NEVER pass objects like
    `Circle` or arrays as JSX attributes.
-   **CF9 — `mapId` Requirement:** `<Map mapId="…">` is **mandatory** whenever
    you render `AdvancedMarkerElement`. Without it, markers silently fail to
    appear. Use a valid Cloud-styled map ID or `"DEMO_MAP_ID"`. Conversely,
    **MUST NOT** pass an arbitrary/unregistered `mapId` when not using advanced
    markers, as it will throw `ApiProjectMapError` and crash the map.
-   **CF10 — Locale & Region:** For international apps, explicitly set
    `language` and `region` on the loader or `<APIProvider>`. Otherwise, results
    are biased to the IP's locale.
-   **CF11 — Avoid `gmpx-*` Extended Component Library:** If MCP returns samples
    using `<gmpx-store-locator>` or similar `gmpx-*` Lit components, **do not
    use them**. They wrap the deprecated Places library. Re-query MCP with
    `"using Places API (New)"` to get current patterns.

5. Critical Failures (CF)

Violating ANY of these causes a silent failure or crash. You must check this list before writing Google Maps Platform code, and verify against it again before concluding your response.

  • CF1 — The CORS Trap: REST endpoints for Routes, Places API (New), Address Validation, and Geocoding lack permissive CORS headers. Client-side fetch() to googleapis.com is BLOCKED. ALWAYS use official SDK wrappers (e.g., importLibrary('places') or useMapsLibrary(...)) or a server-side proxy.
  • CF2 — Map Height Collapse: <Map> and <gmp-map> need explicit CSS height (e.g., height: 100vh or height: 100% on a sized parent). Otherwise, they silently render at 0×0.
  • CF3 — Headless GPU/WebGL Gotchas: Headless testing and screenshot environments typically have no WebGL support. GPU-dependent features (Photorealistic 3D, deck.gl) will fail to render (throwing WebGL2 is not available).
  • CF4 — Cross-Platform Framework Rules: Proactively recommend wrapping WebGL/JS implementations in a custom WebView container for advanced Photorealistic 3D Map Tiles rather than attempting native wrapper bridges (which do not support them).
  • CF5 — Framework Policy:
    • React: MUST use @vis.gl/react-google-maps. Never use google-map-react or @react-google-maps/api.
    • Angular: MUST use @angular/google-maps.
    • Vanilla JS: Use @googlemaps/js-api-loader (setOptions + importLibrary).
  • CF6 — LatLng Trap: Prefer POJO {lat, lng} literals. If a class instance is required, use new google.maps.LatLng(lat, lng). Note that LatLng lives in importLibrary("core"), NOT "maps".
  • CF7 — Deprecated PinElement & Marker Composition:
    • PinElement.element and PinElement.glyph are deprecated. Use PinElement directly, and PinElementOptions.glyphText / glyphSrc.
    • For custom HTML inside an AdvancedMarkerElement, prefer marker.append(htmlElement) over assigning to the .content setter.
    • Click handling: gmp-click event + gmpClickable: true are only available on the v=beta channel. On weekly, fall back to listening for plain 'click' on the marker element.
  • CF8 — Web Component Property-vs-Attribute Trap (React): React stringifies JSX props into HTML attributes; it does NOT pass complex objects to Web Components. For Google Maps Platform web components (e.g. PlaceAutocompleteElement), mount imperatively with useRef + useEffect and assign properties on the DOM element directly. NEVER pass objects like Circle or arrays as JSX attributes.
  • CF9 — mapId Requirement: <Map mapId="…"> is mandatory whenever you render AdvancedMarkerElement. Without it, markers silently fail to appear. Use a valid Cloud-styled map ID or "DEMO_MAP_ID". Conversely, MUST NOT pass an arbitrary/unregistered mapId when not using advanced markers, as it will throw ApiProjectMapError and crash the map.
  • CF10 — Locale & Region: For international apps, explicitly set language and region on the loader or <APIProvider>. Otherwise, results are biased to the IP's locale.
  • CF11 — Avoid gmpx-* Extended Component Library: If MCP returns samples using <gmpx-store-locator> or similar gmpx-* Lit components, do not use them. They wrap the deprecated Places library. Re-query MCP with "using Places API (New)" to get current patterns.

7. Credentials Setup & Demo Key Quickstart

Select the correct authentication model based on the product.

  • API Key: Used for most Maps SDKs and REST APIs (covers Maps JS, Places, Routes, Geocoding, Address Validation, Geolocation, Time Zone, Elevation, Roads, Static Maps, Street View Static, Maps Embed, Air Quality, Pollen, Solar, Weather, Aerial View render endpoint).
  • OAuth / Application Default Credentials (ADC): Required for Route Optimization API, Map Tiles session tokens, Places Aggregate API, Mobility/Fleet Engine, and Aerial View management. Do not use API keys for these endpoints (they will return a 401 Unauthorized error). Flag this clearly to the user and request the secret if needed. Refer to the corresponding sub-skill for details.

Production: Standard API Keys

  • Provisioning: Direct the user to get a key from the Google Cloud Console.
  • Environment: NEVER hardcode the API key in the generated code. Always instruct the user to store it via environment variables (e.g., .env). Tell the user exactly which Cloud APIs they need to enable for the feature you built.
  • Security: You MUST remind the user to restrict their production key by HTTP referrer (Web), Package Name (Android), or Bundle ID (iOS), and to limit the key to specific APIs to prevent quota scraping.

Demo Key Quickstart

When a developer has not yet configured their Google Cloud project or billing account, recommend the Maps Demo Key as the lowest-friction path for prototyping — no billing account and no Cloud project setup required. It is NOT zero-effort: the user must still sign in and click through a short console flow to mint the key, then paste it back to you. Set that expectation up front rather than implying the key is instant.

  • What the user actually has to do (walk them through these steps explicitly):
    1. Open https://mapsplatform.google.com/maps-demo-key?utm_campaign=gmp_git_agentskills_v1.

    4. Click the button to generate / reveal the demo key.
    5. Copy the key and paste it back so it can be stored as a secret/environment variable (see "Agent behavior" below).
  • Agent behavior: Do NOT hardcode the key or block silently. Request it from the user as a secret/env var (e.g. GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY) using the host environment's secret-request mechanism, and pause until they provide it. Tell them which env var name you expect. While waiting, you may finish all non-key work (UI, server, routing proxy) so the app runs the moment the key lands.
  • Currently supported APIs (as of Jan 2025 — fetch the latest supported list if the user requests an API not listed here): Maps JavaScript API, Places API, Routes API, Geocoding API, Weather API, Maps Grounding Lite, Places UI Kit.
  • Limits & Constraints: Warn the user that it has a daily reset limit, is NOT for production usage, and is governed by the distinct Maps Demo Project Terms of Service.

8. Required Response Verification

Any task that produces Google Maps Platform code is not complete until the appendix below has been shown to the user in your final, user-facing message. "At the conclusion of a response" is not enough — treat the appendix as a completion gate, not an optional footer.

Delegation clause (read this first). If implementation is delegated to a subagent, the orchestrating agent remains responsible for surfacing this appendix to the user. A subagent's internal appendix does not satisfy this requirement — re-state it in your own final message. This is the most common way the appendix gets dropped. For multi-step or long sessions, present the appendix once per session (after the Google Maps Platform work is delivered) rather than after every individual interaction. However, for very long ongoing sessions, ensure the appendix is presented at least once every 24 hours.

Code Requirement

  • Source Attribution Comment: If you copy code verbatim (or near-verbatim) from official Google Maps Platform docs or sample repos, you MUST add this comment to the top of the file: // Source: Google Maps Platform Code Assist. (Do not apply this to merely adapted or agent-authored code).

Google Sheets

Work with a Google Sheet the user names or links to. Everything here assumes you already have the spreadsheet ID — the segment between /d/ and /edit in a https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<SPREADSHEET_ID>/edit URL.

[!CAUTION]

mutate delete-sheet, mutate delete-rows, mutate delete-cols, and mutate clear permanently remove data. Never run a destructive command the user did not explicitly ask for.

mutate delete permanently deletes an entire spreadsheet document. Never use it unless the user asks explicitly; ask for confirmation and wait for the answer before executing. The command also requires --confirm.

Never share a spreadsheet with a broad audience, a public link, or a whole organization. The user already has access to anything created on their behalf — let them handle sharing unless they explicitly instruct otherwise.

Setup and Authentication

gsheets auth status is the only way to tell whether you are logged in. Do not run --help, search the filesystem or environment for tokens, check another plugin's login, or run an operational command before logging in. Follow these steps exactly.

1. Register and check. Run this skill's script with auth status. It downloads the CLI, registers gsheets on the agent's PATH (not the user's shell), and reports whether you are logged in:

<path/to/this/skill>/scripts/gsheets auth status

# Windows (PowerShell)
& "<path\to\this\skill>\scripts\gsheets.cmd" auth status

Every later call is just gsheets. Never ask the user to run it; they cannot. If it reports Logged in, you are ready.

2. Log in for the user. Start this as a background command:

gsheets auth login

It prints an authorization URL and exits on its own once the user approves. Read the URL from the task's log, open it in the user's browser or hand them the link, then stop and wait. Confirm with gsheets auth status.

Usage

Do every Google Sheets operation — reading, writing, formatting, creating, exporting — through gsheets. Commands are split into two namespaces: readonly for anything that only reads, mutate for anything that changes the spreadsheet. Run gsheets --help, or gsheets <namespace> <command> --help, to confirm the exact flags of any command below.

Two rules the CLI's own help will not tell you:

  • Never run a destructive command the user did not ask for. Deleting a spreadsheet, a sheet, or rows, and clearing a range, all discard data with no undo on the user's side. Ask first and wait for an answer.
  • Write the narrowest range that does the job. Rewriting a whole sheet to change a few cells destroys formatting, formulas, and validation rules that were never yours to touch.

Recipes

Read data (readonly):

gsheets readonly read SPREADSHEET_ID 'Sheet1!A1:D10'
gsheets readonly read-all SPREADSHEET_ID
gsheets readonly read-links SPREADSHEET_ID 'Sheet1!A1:D10'   # embedded hyperlinks, rich-text links, and smart chips
gsheets readonly info SPREADSHEET_ID
gsheets readonly list-sheets SPREADSHEET_ID
gsheets readonly list-named-ranges SPREADSHEET_ID
gsheets readonly list-filter-views SPREADSHEET_ID
gsheets readonly list "Quarterly Results"                    # search spreadsheets in Drive
gsheets readonly list-revisions SPREADSHEET_ID               # revision history
gsheets readonly inspect-cell SPREADSHEET_ID 'Sheet1!B4'     # deep cell and error diagnostics
gsheets readonly get-settings SPREADSHEET_ID                 # locale and timezone properties
gsheets readonly list-comments SPREADSHEET_ID                # comment threads and replies

Write data (mutate):

gsheets mutate write SPREADSHEET_ID 'Sheet1!A1:B2' "Name,Age|Alice,30"
gsheets mutate write SPREADSHEET_ID 'Sheet1!A1:B2' $'Name,Age\nAlice,30'
gsheets mutate write SPREADSHEET_ID 'Sheet1!A1' "Value with\, a comma"
gsheets mutate append SPREADSHEET_ID 'Sheet1!A1' "Bob,25"
gsheets mutate clear SPREADSHEET_ID 'Sheet1!A1:D10'
gsheets mutate import-csv SPREADSHEET_ID /path/to/data.csv
gsheets mutate find-replace SPREADSHEET_ID --find "old" --replace "new"
gsheets mutate notes SPREADSHEET_ID 'Sheet1!A1' "This is a note"
gsheets mutate add-comment SPREADSHEET_ID "This is a comment" --range 'Sheet1!A1:A1'
gsheets mutate reply-comment SPREADSHEET_ID COMMENT_ID "This is a reply"
gsheets mutate resolve-comment SPREADSHEET_ID COMMENT_ID "Optional resolve message"

Create, delete, copy, and rename (mutate):

gsheets mutate create --title "New Spreadsheet"
gsheets mutate delete SPREADSHEET_ID --confirm                       # permanently deletes the document
gsheets mutate rename SPREADSHEET_ID "New File Name"
gsheets mutate copy-spreadsheet SPREADSHEET_ID "Copy Title"
gsheets mutate add-sheet SPREADSHEET_ID --title "Sheet2"
gsheets mutate delete-sheet SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 1
gsheets mutate rename-sheet SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --title "Main"
gsheets mutate copy-sheet SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --dest OTHER_SPREADSHEET_ID
gsheets mutate create-from-template TEMPLATE_ID --title "New" --replacements "{{NAME}}=Alice"

Formatting (mutate):

gsheets mutate format SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --start-row 0 --end-row 1 --start-col 0 --end-col 5 --bold --align CENTER --bg-color "#00FF00" --fg-color "#FF0000" --wrap
gsheets mutate set-col-width SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --start-col 0 --end-col 1 --pixels 200
gsheets mutate autosize SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --start-col 0 --end-col 5
gsheets mutate merge SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --start-row 0 --end-row 1 --start-col 0 --end-col 3
gsheets mutate unmerge SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --start-row 0 --end-row 1 --start-col 0 --end-col 3
gsheets mutate freeze SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --rows 1 --cols 1
gsheets mutate borders SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --style SOLID --color "#000000"
gsheets mutate conditional-format SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --start-row 0 --end-row 100 --start-col 0 --end-col 1 --condition NUMBER_GREATER --value "90" --color "#00FF00"

Rows, columns, and data operations (mutate):

gsheets mutate sort SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --col 0                 # --asc is default, omit for descending
gsheets mutate insert-rows SPREADSHEET_ID --range 'Sheet1!5:10'         # human-readable ranges work
gsheets mutate delete-rows SPREADSHEET_ID --range 'Sheet1!5:10'
gsheets mutate insert-cols SPREADSHEET_ID --range 'Sheet1!C:D'
gsheets mutate insert-cols SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --start 2 --count 3 --inherit-from-before   # append at the end (start may equal grid size)
gsheets mutate delete-cols SPREADSHEET_ID --range 'Sheet1!C:D'
gsheets mutate copy-paste SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --start-row 0 --end-row 5 --start-col 0 --end-col 2 --dest-row 0 --dest-col 3 --paste-type PASTE_VALUES
gsheets mutate auto-fill SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --start-row 0 --end-row 10 --start-col 0 --end-col 1 --source-end-row 3
gsheets mutate smart-fill SPREADSHEET_ID 'Sheet1!B2'                    # fills down the adjacent contiguous depth
gsheets mutate formula-fill SPREADSHEET_ID --range 'Sheet1!C1:C10' --formula "=B1+A1"   # shifts relative references
gsheets mutate data-validation SPREADSHEET_ID 'Sheet1!B1:B10' --values "Yes,No,Maybe"
gsheets mutate protect SPREADSHEET_ID --range 'Sheet1!A1:D1' --editors "alice@example.com,bob@example.com"
gsheets mutate change-settings SPREADSHEET_ID --locale "de_DE" --timezone "Europe/Berlin"
gsheets mutate add-named-range SPREADSHEET_ID "MyRange" 'Sheet1!A1:D10'
gsheets mutate add-filter-view SPREADSHEET_ID "MyFilter" --sheet-id 0
gsheets mutate delete-filter-view SPREADSHEET_ID 12345

Charts, pivots, tables, sharing, and export:

gsheets mutate add-chart SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --chart-type BAR --start-row 0 --end-row 10 --start-col 0 --end-col 2 --title "Sales"
gsheets mutate add-chart SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --chart-type COLUMN --start-row 0 --end-row 10 --start-col 0 --end-col 2 --title "Pillars" --overlay --colors "#4285F4,#EA4335"
gsheets readonly export-chart SPREADSHEET_ID --chart-id 1 --output /tmp/chart.png
gsheets mutate pivot SPREADSHEET_ID --source 'Sheet1!A1:D100' --target-sheet-id 0
gsheets readonly export SPREADSHEET_ID /tmp/export.csv --format csv
gsheets readonly export SPREADSHEET_ID /tmp/export_tab.csv --format csv --sheet "Sheet2"   # specific tab (CSV/TSV only)
gsheets readonly export SPREADSHEET_ID /tmp/page1.png --format png --page 1
gsheets mutate share SPREADSHEET_ID --email user@example.com --role writer
gsheets mutate add-table SPREADSHEET_ID "MyTable" 'Sheet1!A1:D10'
gsheets mutate update-table SPREADSHEET_ID "MyTable" 'Sheet1!A1:D20'
gsheets mutate delete-table SPREADSHEET_ID "MyTable"
gsheets mutate batch SPREADSHEET_ID -f requests.json
gsheets mutate raw-batch SPREADSHEET_ID -f raw_requests.json

Batch operations file (requests.json):

Each op is one of read, write, append, or clear. For write and append, the data field is required and must be a 2D array of rows ([[...]]). Unknown JSON fields are rejected — typos surface immediately rather than silently producing no-op writes.

[
  {"op": "read",   "range": "Sheet1!A1:B2"},
  {"op": "write",  "range": "Sheet1!A1",     "data": [["Critical", "High"]]},
  {"op": "append", "range": "Sheet1!A1",     "data": [["new row"]]},
  {"op": "clear",  "range": "Sheet1!A1:B2"}
]

[!IMPORTANT]

The field is data, not values. Writing "values": "X" fails with parsing batch JSON: json: unknown field "values". This is deliberate: the field name that used to be silently accepted was a silent-data-loss footgun.

Commands

Tips

  • Creating Spreadsheets with Specific Tabs: When creating a new spreadsheet with a specific tab/sheet name, note that mutate create generates a default initial tab ("Sheet 1", --sheet-id 0). You can either repurpose "Sheet 1" by renaming it (mutate rename-sheet SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --title "Desired Tab Name") or add the new sheet and delete "Sheet 1" (mutate delete-sheet SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0).
  • CRITICAL: Never attempt to scrape Google Sheets URLs (e.g., docs.google.com/spreadsheets/...) using web reading tools. Always use the GSheets CLI commands (readonly read, readonly read-all) to access spreadsheet contents, as the URLs require authentication and will return permission errors.
  • LIMITATION: Due to Google Sheets API and Drive API limitations, any comment created programmatically using mutate add-comment with a cell range anchor will appear as "Original Content Deleted" (unanchored) in the Google Sheets grid Web UI. However, the comment remains fully visible in the Sheets "Comment History" sidebar, and it is queryable/writable via the CLI's list-comments, reply-comment, and resolve-comment commands.
  • The mutate format command uses --sheet-id, --start-row/--end-row, --start-col/--end-col (not A1 range notation)
  • The mutate notes command takes range and note text as positional arguments (not --set flag)
  • Avoid spaces in sheet names when used in range notation; if unavoidable, wrap in single quotes: "'My Sheet'!A1:B5"
  • Chart types: BAR, LINE, AREA work reliably; PIE is listed but not supported by the API
  • Use --json on read commands to get machine-parseable output
  • Use --markdown-links on readonly read-all to extract rich-text hyperlinks and Smart Chips (Rich Links and People Chips) embedded in cells. Without this flag, the API returns only the display text, and hidden link targets or smart chip URIs are lost. With the flag, both standard links and smart chips (including People Chips as mailto: links) are rendered as [display text](URL). Can be combined with --json to output an array of rows containing the markdown-formatted strings.
  • readonly read-links RANGE is the dedicated command (vs the --markdown-links flag above, which is scoped to read-all) to pull embedded hyperlinks, rich-text links, and Smart Chips (Rich Links and People Chips as mailto: links) from a specific range, rendered as [display text](URL). Add --json for an array of rows, or --debug-cell to dump the raw CellData JSON for troubleshooting.
  • Use --value-render-option FORMULA on the readonly read command to retrieve the underlying cell formulas instead of the evaluated values.
  • readonly export supports csv, xlsx, pdf, ods, tsv, and png formats. When exporting to csv or tsv, you can use the --sheet "TabName" flag to export a specific sheet tab by name (by default, Drive CSV export only downloads the first tab).
  • Both | and \n (newline) work as row delimiters in mutate write and mutate append commands. Use | for inline values and $'\n' for multi-row shell input
  • To include a comma inside a cell value, escape it with a backslash: \,
  • batch requires data (not values) for write/append ops; unknown fields are rejected by the strict JSON decoder. See "Batch operations file" above.
  • conditional-format --condition NUMBER_BETWEEN (and NUMBER_NOT_BETWEEN, DATE_BETWEEN, DATE_NOT_BETWEEN) accept a comma-separated --value pair, e.g. --value "1,10". Other conditions still take a single --value. For bands of multiple ranges (e.g. 1-2, 3-5, 6+), add one rule per band.
  • Recommended workflow: Use readonly export SPREADSHEET_ID page.png --format png --page N to export a specific page as an image, review it visually, then iterate on edits

Global Flags

  • --json — output as JSON (works with all read commands)
  • -v, --version — print the CLI build version
  • --legacy-mode — how deprecated/renamed commands are handled: allowed | deprecated (default) | banned


**Batch operations file (`requests.json`):**

Each op is one of `read`, `write`, `append`, or `clear`. For `write` and
`append`, the `data` field is **required** and must be a 2D array of rows
(`[[...]]`). Unknown JSON fields are rejected — typos surface immediately rather
than silently producing no-op writes.

```json
[
  {"op": "read",   "range": "Sheet1!A1:B2"},
  {"op": "write",  "range": "Sheet1!A1",     "data": [["Critical", "High"]]},
  {"op": "append", "range": "Sheet1!A1",     "data": [["new row"]]},
  {"op": "clear",  "range": "Sheet1!A1:B2"}
]
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> The field is `data`, not `values`. Writing `"values": "X"` fails with `parsing
> batch JSON: json: unknown field "values"`. This is deliberate: the field name
> that used to be silently accepted was a silent-data-loss footgun.

## Tips

-   **Creating Spreadsheets with Specific Tabs:** When creating a new
    spreadsheet with a specific tab/sheet name, note that `mutate create`
    generates a default initial tab ("Sheet 1", `--sheet-id 0`). You can either
    repurpose "Sheet 1" by renaming it (`mutate rename-sheet SPREADSHEET_ID
    --sheet-id 0 --title "Desired Tab Name"`) or add the new sheet and delete
    "Sheet 1" (`mutate delete-sheet SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0`).
-   **CRITICAL:** Never attempt to scrape Google Sheets URLs (e.g.,
    `docs.google.com/spreadsheets/...`) using web reading tools. Always use the
    GSheets CLI commands (`readonly read`, `readonly read-all`) to access
    spreadsheet contents, as the URLs require authentication and will return
    permission errors.
-   **LIMITATION:** Due to Google Sheets API and Drive API limitations, any
    comment created programmatically using `mutate add-comment` with a cell
    range anchor will appear as "Original Content Deleted" (unanchored) in the
    Google Sheets grid Web UI. However, the comment remains fully visible in the
    Sheets "Comment History" sidebar, and it is queryable/writable via the CLI's
    `list-comments`, `reply-comment`, and `resolve-comment` commands.
-   The `mutate format` command uses `--sheet-id`, `--start-row/--end-row`,
    `--start-col/--end-col` (not A1 range notation)
-   The `mutate notes` command takes range and note text as positional arguments
    (not --set flag)
-   Avoid spaces in sheet names when used in range notation; if unavoidable,
    wrap in single quotes: `"'My Sheet'!A1:B5"`
-   Chart types: `BAR`, `LINE`, `AREA` work reliably; `PIE` is listed but not
    supported by the API
-   Use `--json` on read commands to get machine-parseable output
-   Use `--markdown-links` on `readonly read-all` to extract rich-text
    hyperlinks and Smart Chips (Rich Links and People Chips) embedded in cells.
    Without this flag, the API returns only the display text, and hidden link
    targets or smart chip URIs are lost. With the flag, both standard links and
    smart chips (including People Chips as `mailto:` links) are rendered as
    `[display text](URL)`. Can be combined with `--json` to output an array of
    rows containing the markdown-formatted strings.
-   `readonly read-links RANGE` is the dedicated command (vs the
    `--markdown-links` flag above, which is scoped to `read-all`) to pull
    embedded hyperlinks, rich-text links, and Smart Chips (Rich Links and People
    Chips as `mailto:` links) from a specific range, rendered as `[display
    text](URL)`. Add `--json` for an array of rows, or `--debug-cell` to dump
    the raw `CellData` JSON for troubleshooting.
-   Use `--value-render-option FORMULA` on the `readonly read` command to
    retrieve the underlying cell formulas instead of the evaluated values.
-   `readonly export` supports `csv`, `xlsx`, `pdf`, `ods`, `tsv`, and `png`
    formats. When exporting to `csv` or `tsv`, you can use the `--sheet
    "TabName"` flag to export a specific sheet tab by name (by default, Drive
    CSV export only downloads the first tab).
-   Both `|` and `\n` (newline) work as row delimiters in `mutate write` and
    `mutate append` commands. Use `|` for inline values and `$'\n'` for
    multi-row shell input
-   To include a comma inside a cell value, escape it with a backslash: `\,`
-   `batch` requires `data` (not `values`) for `write`/`append` ops; unknown
    fields are rejected by the strict JSON decoder. See "Batch operations file"
    above.
-   `conditional-format --condition NUMBER_BETWEEN` (and `NUMBER_NOT_BETWEEN`,
    `DATE_BETWEEN`, `DATE_NOT_BETWEEN`) accept a comma-separated `--value` pair,
    e.g. `--value "1,10"`. Other conditions still take a single `--value`. For
    bands of multiple ranges (e.g. 1-2, 3-5, 6+), add one rule per band.
-   **Recommended workflow:** Use `readonly export SPREADSHEET_ID page.png
    --format png --page N` to export a specific page as an image, review it
    visually, then iterate on edits

## Global Flags

-   `--json` — output as JSON (works with all read commands)
-   `-v`, `--version` — print the CLI build version
-   `--legacy-mode` — how deprecated/renamed commands are handled: `allowed` |
    `deprecated` (default) | `banned`

gsheets mutate add-chart SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --chart-type BAR --start-row 0 --end-row 10 --start-col 0 --end-col 2 --title "Sales"
gsheets mutate add-chart SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --chart-type COLUMN --start-row 0 --end-row 10 --start-col 0 --end-col 2 --title "Pillars" --overlay --colors "#4285F4,#EA4335"
gsheets readonly export-chart SPREADSHEET_ID --chart-id 1 --output /tmp/chart.png
gsheets mutate pivot SPREADSHEET_ID --source 'Sheet1!A1:D100' --target-sheet-id 0
gsheets readonly export SPREADSHEET_ID /tmp/export.csv --format csv
gsheets readonly export SPREADSHEET_ID /tmp/export_tab.csv --format csv --sheet "Sheet2"   # specific tab (CSV/TSV only)
gsheets readonly export SPREADSHEET_ID /tmp/page1.png --format png --page 1
gsheets mutate share SPREADSHEET_ID --email user@example.com --role writer
gsheets mutate add-table SPREADSHEET_ID "MyTable" 'Sheet1!A1:D10'
gsheets mutate update-table SPREADSHEET_ID "MyTable" 'Sheet1!A1:D20'
gsheets mutate delete-table SPREADSHEET_ID "MyTable"
gsheets mutate batch SPREADSHEET_ID -f requests.json
gsheets mutate raw-batch SPREADSHEET_ID -f raw_requests.json

Batch operations file (requests.json):

Each op is one of read, write, append, or clear. For write and append, the data field is required and must be a 2D array of rows ([[...]]). Unknown JSON fields are rejected — typos surface immediately rather than silently producing no-op writes.

[
  {"op": "read",   "range": "Sheet1!A1:B2"},
  {"op": "write",  "range": "Sheet1!A1",     "data": [["Critical", "High"]]},
  {"op": "append", "range": "Sheet1!A1",     "data": [["new row"]]},
  {"op": "clear",  "range": "Sheet1!A1:B2"}
]

[!IMPORTANT]

The field is data, not values. Writing "values": "X" fails with parsing batch JSON: json: unknown field "values". This is deliberate: the field name that used to be silently accepted was a silent-data-loss footgun.

Tips

  • Creating Spreadsheets with Specific Tabs: When creating a new spreadsheet with a specific tab/sheet name, note that mutate create generates a default initial tab ("Sheet 1", --sheet-id 0). You can either repurpose "Sheet 1" by renaming it (mutate rename-sheet SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0 --title "Desired Tab Name") or add the new sheet and delete "Sheet 1" (mutate delete-sheet SPREADSHEET_ID --sheet-id 0).
  • CRITICAL: Never attempt to scrape Google Sheets URLs (e.g., docs.google.com/spreadsheets/...) using web reading tools. Always use the GSheets CLI commands (readonly read, readonly read-all) to access spreadsheet contents, as the URLs require authentication and will return permission errors.
  • LIMITATION: Due to Google Sheets API and Drive API limitations, any comment created programmatically using mutate add-comment with a cell range anchor will appear as "Original Content Deleted" (unanchored) in the Google Sheets grid Web UI. However, the comment remains fully visible in the Sheets "Comment History" sidebar, and it is queryable/writable via the CLI's list-comments, reply-comment, and resolve-comment commands.
  • The mutate format command uses --sheet-id, --start-row/--end-row, --start-col/--end-col (not A1 range notation)
  • The mutate notes command takes range and note text as positional arguments (not --set flag)
  • Avoid spaces in sheet names when used in range notation; if unavoidable, wrap in single quotes: "'My Sheet'!A1:B5"
  • Chart types: BAR, LINE, AREA work reliably; PIE is listed but not supported by the API
  • Use --json on read commands to get machine-parseable output
  • Use --markdown-links on readonly read-all to extract rich-text hyperlinks and Smart Chips (Rich Links and People Chips) embedded in cells. Without this flag, the API returns only the display text, and hidden link targets or smart chip URIs are lost. With the flag, both standard links and smart chips (including People Chips as mailto: links) are rendered as [display text](URL). Can be combined with --json to output an array of rows containing the markdown-formatted strings.
  • readonly read-links RANGE is the dedicated command (vs the --markdown-links flag above, which is scoped to read-all) to pull embedded hyperlinks, rich-text links, and Smart Chips (Rich Links and People Chips as mailto: links) from a specific range, rendered as [display text](URL). Add --json for an array of rows, or --debug-cell to dump the raw CellData JSON for troubleshooting.
  • Use --value-render-option FORMULA on the readonly read command to retrieve the underlying cell formulas instead of the evaluated values.
  • readonly export supports csv, xlsx, pdf, ods, tsv, and png formats. When exporting to csv or tsv, you can use the --sheet "TabName" flag to export a specific sheet tab by name (by default, Drive CSV export only downloads the first tab).
  • Both | and \n (newline) work as row delimiters in mutate write and mutate append commands. Use | for inline values and $'\n' for multi-row shell input
  • To include a comma inside a cell value, escape it with a backslash: \,
  • batch requires data (not values) for write/append ops; unknown fields are rejected by the strict JSON decoder. See "Batch operations file" above.
  • conditional-format --condition NUMBER_BETWEEN (and NUMBER_NOT_BETWEEN, DATE_BETWEEN, DATE_NOT_BETWEEN) accept a comma-separated --value pair, e.g. --value "1,10". Other conditions still take a single --value. For bands of multiple ranges (e.g. 1-2, 3-5, 6+), add one rule per band.
  • Recommended workflow: Use readonly export SPREADSHEET_ID page.png --format png --page N to export a specific page as an image, review it visually, then iterate on edits

Global Flags

  • --json — output as JSON (works with all read commands)
  • -v, --version — print the CLI build version
  • --legacy-mode — how deprecated/renamed commands are handled: allowed | deprecated (default) | banned

Google Slides

Work with a Google Slides presentation the user names or links to. Everything here assumes you already have the presentation ID — the segment between /d/ and /edit in a https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/<PRESENTATION_ID>/edit URL.

Setup and Authentication

gslides auth status is the only way to tell whether you are logged in. Do not run --help, search the filesystem or environment for tokens, check another plugin's login, or run an operational command before logging in. Follow these steps exactly.

1. Register and check. Run this skill's script with auth status. It downloads the CLI, registers gslides on the agent's PATH (not the user's shell), and reports whether you are logged in:

<path/to/this/skill>/scripts/gslides auth status

# Windows (PowerShell)
& "<path\to\this\skill>\scripts\gslides.cmd" auth status

Every later call is just gslides. Never ask the user to run it; they cannot. If it reports Logged in, you are ready.

2. Log in for the user. Start this as a background command:

gslides auth login

It prints an authorization URL and exits on its own once the user approves. Read the URL from the task's log, open it in the user's browser or hand them the link, then stop and wait. Confirm with gslides auth status.

Usage

Do every Google Slides operation — reading, creating, editing, exporting, extracting images — through gslides. Run gslides --help to discover the available commands and their flags.

Two rules the CLI's own help will not tell you:

  • Never delete a slide the user did not ask you to delete. A removed slide takes its speaker notes and layout with it, and the user cannot get them back.
  • Edit the elements you were asked about, not the whole deck. Rebuilding a slide from scratch loses the theme, placeholder wiring, and notes that made it consistent with the rest of the presentation.

[!CAUTION]

gslides mutate delete-slide and gslides mutate delete-element permanently remove content from a presentation. Never run a destructive command unless the user explicitly asks.

Never share a presentation with a broad audience, a public link, or a whole organization. The user already has access to anything created on their behalf — let them handle sharing unless they explicitly instruct otherwise.

Recipes

Read and inspect:

gslides readonly read PRESENTATION_ID               # all slides as text (or --json for presentation AST)
gslides readonly read-all PRESENTATION_ID           # all slides as text (or --json for presentation AST)
gslides readonly info PRESENTATION_ID               # presentation metadata (or --json for full presentation AST)
gslides readonly list-slides PRESENTATION_ID        # list slides (or --json for slides array)
gslides readonly list-elements PRESENTATION_ID SLIDE_ID
gslides readonly get-page PRESENTATION_ID SLIDE_ID
gslides readonly get-notes PRESENTATION_ID SLIDE_ID
gslides readonly extract-images PRESENTATION_ID

Create and organize:

gslides mutate create --title "My Presentation"
gslides mutate copy PRESENTATION_ID "Copy Title"
gslides mutate add-slide PRESENTATION_ID
gslides mutate duplicate PRESENTATION_ID SLIDE_ID
gslides mutate delete-slide PRESENTATION_ID SLIDE_ID
gslides mutate reorder-slide PRESENTATION_ID SLIDE_ID --position 0

Add content:

gslides mutate add-textbox PRESENTATION_ID --slide SLIDE_ID --text "Hello" --x 100 --y 100 --width 300 --height 50 --content-alignment MIDDLE
gslides mutate add-text PRESENTATION_ID "More text" --textbox ELEMENT_ID
gslides mutate update-text PRESENTATION_ID --element ELEMENT_ID --text "New text"
gslides mutate add-image PRESENTATION_ID --slide SLIDE_ID --url "https://..." --x 100 --y 200 --width 200 --height 150
gslides mutate insert-image-from-file PRESENTATION_ID --slide SLIDE_ID --file /path/to/image.png
gslides mutate add-table PRESENTATION_ID --slide SLIDE_ID --rows 3 --cols 4
gslides mutate set-table-cell PRESENTATION_ID --table TABLE_ID --row 0 --col 0 --text "Header"
gslides mutate delete-element PRESENTATION_ID ELEMENT_ID
gslides mutate move-element PRESENTATION_ID ELEMENT_ID --x 200 --y 150
gslides mutate resize-element PRESENTATION_ID ELEMENT_ID --width 400 --height 300
gslides mutate update-shape PRESENTATION_ID --element ELEMENT_ID --text "New text" --background-color "#FF0000" --bold

Styling and export:

gslides mutate set-background PRESENTATION_ID --slide SLIDE_ID --color "#4285F4"
gslides mutate set-notes PRESENTATION_ID --slide SLIDE_ID --text "Speaker notes here"
gslides readonly export PRESENTATION_ID /tmp/pres.pdf --format pdf
gslides readonly export-thumbnail PRESENTATION_ID /tmp/slide.png
gslides mutate share PRESENTATION_ID --email user@example.com --role writer
gslides mutate batch PRESENTATION_ID requests.json

Tips

  • CRITICAL: Never attempt to scrape Google Slides URLs (e.g., docs.google.com/presentation/...) using web reading tools. Always use the GSlides CLI commands (gslides readonly read, gslides readonly read-all) to access presentation contents, as the URLs require authentication and will return permission errors.

  • gslides mutate set-table-cell and gslides mutate set-notes safely handle empty content (no need to pre-populate)

  • Use gslides readonly list-elements PRES_ID SLIDE_INDEX to discover element IDs for tables, textboxes, etc. The SLIDE_INDEX is 0-based (0=first slide, 1=second, etc.)

  • Reordering slides index shift: When using gslides mutate reorder-slide, the --position (which maps to InsertionIndex in Slides API) is evaluated before the source slide is removed.

    • If moving a slide to a later position (source < target): specify position = target + 1 to make it end up at index target. (e.g., to move Slide 4 (index 3) to end up at index 15, use --position 16).
    • If moving a slide to an earlier position (source > target): specify position = target to make it end up at index target.

  • The gslides mutate batch command reads a JSON file of operations for efficient bulk updates. Use --file - to pipe from stdin.

  • Removing Default Slide Elements: Newly created presentations (via gslides mutate create) contain a single title slide p with default placeholders (centered title i0 and subtitle i1). To start with a completely blank first slide, delete them at the beginning of your batch JSON file:

    [
  {"op": "delete-element", "element": "i0"},
  {"op": "delete-element", "element": "i1"}
]

  • Recommended workflow: Use gslides readonly export-thumbnail PRES_ID output.png --slide SLIDE_ID to export a slide as an image, review it visually, then iterate. This is the best way to verify layout, colors, and readability before sharing. Note: --slide takes a slide object ID (e.g. p, slide_xxx), not a 0-based index. Use gslides mutate batch --json or gslides readonly list-slides --json to get slide IDs.

Placeholder IDs (Single-Batch Workflows)

Use "id" on add-slide and add-table to create placeholder IDs that subsequent ops can reference within the same batch:

[
  {"op":"add-slide","layout":"BLANK","id":"SLIDE_1"},
  {"op":"set-background","slide":"SLIDE_1","color":"#1E2761"},
  {"op":"add-table","slide":"SLIDE_1","rows":3,"cols":3,"id":"TABLE_1"},
  {"op":"set-table-cell","table":"TABLE_1","row":0,"col":0,"text":"Header"}
]

This eliminates the need for multi-pass workflows. The CLI resolves placeholders to API-generated IDs at runtime.

set-notes for newly-created slides is automatically deferred to a second API call (the CLI handles this transparently).

Batch --json Response

Use gslides mutate batch PRES_ID -f file.json --json to get created IDs. The resolved_ids map is needed for any follow-up commands (e.g. gslides readonly export-thumbnail, gslides mutate insert-image-from-file) that target created slides:

{"operations":12,"api_requests":30,"created_slides":["slide_xxx"],"created_tables":["table_xxx"],"resolved_ids":{"SLIDE_1":"slide_xxx","TABLE_1":"table_xxx"}}

Card Design Tips (from Testing)

  • Use header + body combo — two textboxes (bold 20pt header + 13-14pt body) instead of one tall card. This avoids empty space and gives visual hierarchy.
  • Accent dividers: thin rectangles (3-4px height) between card sections add polish.
  • Bottom taglines: centered muted text below cards fills vertical whitespace.
  • Stat call-outs: rounded rectangles with big numbers (36pt+) make overview slides more visual.

Key Features

  • background_color: Sets shape fill on textboxes and shapes (card layouts, visual accents). Can be set to "transparent" to remove fill color.

  • alpha: Sets fill opacity (0.0 to 1.0, e.g. 0.85 for 85% opacity) on shape, textbox, and table cell background colors.

  • outline_color: Hex color (e.g., "#FF0000") to style the shape's outline/border.

  • outline_weight: Line weight in points (e.g. 1.5) for the shape's outline/border.

  • font_family: Set font (e.g., "Roboto", "Montserrat", "Oswald")

  • link: Add hyperlinks to text

  • strikethrough: Applies strikethrough styling to text (boolean, e.g. true)

  • line_spacing: Set line height (percentage, e.g., 150 = 1.5× spacing)

  • start/end: Style a range of text (not just all text) in style-text

  • content_alignment: Vertical text alignment inside shape/textbox. Allowed values: "TOP", "MIDDLE", "BOTTOM".

  • line_category: Type of line to create (e.g. "STRAIGHT", "BENT", "CURVED", defaults to "STRAIGHT").

  • start_arrow / end_arrow: Arrowhead style (e.g. "NONE", "FILL_ARROW", "STEALTH_ARROW", "CHEVRON_ARROW", "DIAMOND_ARROW", defaults to "NONE").

  • line_weight: Line weight/thickness in points (e.g. 2.5).

  • dash_style: Line dash pattern (e.g. "SOLID", "DASH", "DOT", "DASH_DOT", "LONG_DASH", "LONG_DASH_DOT").

  • start_connect / end_connect: Element ID of a shape to anchor each end of the line to, turning it into a connector that auto-routes and stays attached as shapes move. Accepts real element IDs (from gslides readonly list-elements) or in-batch placeholder IDs. When either is set, line_category defaults to "BENT".

  • start_site / end_site: Connection site (edge midpoint) index on the connected shape: 0 = Top, 1 = Left, 2 = Bottom, 3 = Right (verified for RECTANGLE/ROUND_RECTANGLE). A left-to-right connector uses start_site: 3, end_site: 1.

  • updateTableColumnProperties: Update column widths for a table by passing columnIndices and tableColumnProperties.columnWidth:

    {
  "op": "updateTableColumnProperties",
  "updateTableColumnProperties": {
    "objectId": "TABLE_1",
    "columnIndices": [0],
    "tableColumnProperties": {
      "columnWidth": {"magnitude": 65, "unit": "PT"}
    },
    "fields": "columnWidth"
  }
}

Slide Creation Recipe

  1. Outline: Decide N slides, types (title, content, stat, table, closing), and palette
  2. Palette: Pick from references/styling.md (Midnight Executive, Ocean Gradient, Cherry Bold, etc.)
  3. Generate batch JSON: All ops in one file, using the sandwich pattern (dark → light → dark)
  4. Execute: gslides mutate create then gslides mutate batch PRES_ID -f batch.json
  5. Review: gslides readonly export-thumbnail each slide, review PNG
  6. Fix: Second batch or individual commands
  7. Notes: Include set-notes in batch for every slide
  8. Share: gslides mutate share PRES_ID --email ...

# Google Slides

Work with a Google Slides presentation the user names or links to. Everything
here assumes you already have the **presentation ID** — the segment between
`/d/` and `/edit` in a
`https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/<PRESENTATION_ID>/edit` URL.

## Setup and Authentication

`gslides auth status` is the only way to tell whether you are logged in. Do not
run `--help`, search the filesystem or environment for tokens, check another
plugin's login, or run an operational command before logging in. Follow these
steps exactly.

**1. Register and check.** Run this skill's script with `auth status`. It
downloads the CLI, registers `gslides` on the agent's `PATH` (not the user's
shell), and reports whether you are logged in:

```bash
<path/to/this/skill>/scripts/gslides auth status
```

```powershell
# Windows (PowerShell)
& "<path\to\this\skill>\scripts\gslides.cmd" auth status
```

Every later call is just `gslides`. Never ask the user to run it; they cannot.
If it reports `Logged in`, you are ready.

**2. Log in for the user.** Start this as a background command:

```bash
gslides auth login
```

It prints an authorization URL and exits on its own once the user approves. Read
the URL from the task's log, open it in the user's browser or hand them the
link, then stop and wait. Confirm with `gslides auth status`.

## Usage

Do every Google Slides operation — reading, creating, editing, exporting,
extracting images — through `gslides`. Run `gslides --help` to discover the
available commands and their flags.

Two rules the CLI's own help will not tell you:

-   **Never delete a slide the user did not ask you to delete.** A removed slide
    takes its speaker notes and layout with it, and the user cannot get them
    back.
-   **Edit the elements you were asked about, not the whole deck.** Rebuilding a
    slide from scratch loses the theme, placeholder wiring, and notes that made
    it consistent with the rest of the presentation.

> [!CAUTION]
>
> `gslides mutate delete-slide` and `gslides mutate delete-element` permanently
> remove content from a presentation. **Never** run a destructive command unless
> the user explicitly asks.
>
> **Never** share a presentation with a broad audience, a public link, or a
> whole organization. The user already has access to anything created on their
> behalf — let them handle sharing unless they explicitly instruct otherwise.

## Tips

-   **CRITICAL:** Never attempt to scrape Google Slides URLs (e.g.,
    `docs.google.com/presentation/...`) using web reading tools. Always use the
    GSlides CLI commands (`gslides readonly read`, `gslides readonly read-all`)
    to access presentation contents, as the URLs require authentication and will
    return permission errors.
-   `gslides mutate set-table-cell` and `gslides mutate set-notes` safely handle
    empty content (no need to pre-populate)
-   Use `gslides readonly list-elements PRES_ID SLIDE_INDEX` to discover element
    IDs for tables, textboxes, etc. The SLIDE_INDEX is 0-based (0=first slide,
    1=second, etc.)
-   **Reordering slides index shift**: When using `gslides mutate
    reorder-slide`, the `--position` (which maps to `InsertionIndex` in Slides
    API) is evaluated *before* the source slide is removed.
    -   If moving a slide to a *later* position (`source < target`): specify
        `position = target + 1` to make it end up at index `target`. (e.g., to
        move Slide 4 (index 3) to end up at index 15, use `--position 16`).
    -   If moving a slide to an *earlier* position (`source > target`): specify
        `position = target` to make it end up at index `target`.
-   The `gslides mutate batch` command reads a JSON file of operations for
    efficient bulk updates. Use `--file -` to pipe from stdin.
-   **Removing Default Slide Elements:** Newly created presentations (via
    `gslides mutate create`) contain a single title slide `p` with default
    placeholders (centered title `i0` and subtitle `i1`). To start with a
    completely blank first slide, delete them at the beginning of your batch
    JSON file:

    ```json
    [
      {"op": "delete-element", "element": "i0"},
      {"op": "delete-element", "element": "i1"}
    ]
    ```

-   **Recommended workflow:** Use `gslides readonly export-thumbnail PRES_ID
    output.png --slide SLIDE_ID` to export a slide as an image, review it
    visually, then iterate. This is the best way to verify layout, colors, and
    readability before sharing. Note: `--slide` takes a slide **object ID**
    (e.g. `p`, `slide_xxx`), not a 0-based index. Use `gslides mutate batch
    --json` or `gslides readonly list-slides --json` to get slide IDs.

### Placeholder IDs (Single-Batch Workflows)

Use `"id"` on `add-slide` and `add-table` to create placeholder IDs that
subsequent ops can reference **within the same batch**:

```json
[
  {"op":"add-slide","layout":"BLANK","id":"SLIDE_1"},
  {"op":"set-background","slide":"SLIDE_1","color":"#1E2761"},
  {"op":"add-table","slide":"SLIDE_1","rows":3,"cols":3,"id":"TABLE_1"},
  {"op":"set-table-cell","table":"TABLE_1","row":0,"col":0,"text":"Header"}
]
```

This eliminates the need for multi-pass workflows. The CLI resolves placeholders
to API-generated IDs at runtime.

`set-notes` for newly-created slides is automatically deferred to a second API
call (the CLI handles this transparently).

### Batch `--json` Response

Use `gslides mutate batch PRES_ID -f file.json --json` to get created IDs. The
`resolved_ids` map is needed for any follow-up commands (e.g. `gslides readonly
export-thumbnail`, `gslides mutate insert-image-from-file`) that target created
slides:

```json
{"operations":12,"api_requests":30,"created_slides":["slide_xxx"],"created_tables":["table_xxx"],"resolved_ids":{"SLIDE_1":"slide_xxx","TABLE_1":"table_xxx"}}
```

### Card Design Tips (from Testing)

-   **Use header + body combo** — two textboxes (bold 20pt header + 13-14pt
    body) instead of one tall card. This avoids empty space and gives visual
    hierarchy.
-   **Accent dividers**: thin rectangles (3-4px height) between card sections
    add polish.
-   **Bottom taglines**: centered muted text below cards fills vertical
    whitespace.
-   **Stat call-outs**: rounded rectangles with big numbers (36pt+) make
    overview slides more visual.

### Key Features

-   **`background_color`**: Sets shape fill on textboxes and shapes (card
    layouts, visual accents). Can be set to `"transparent"` to remove fill
    color.
-   **`alpha`**: Sets fill opacity (0.0 to 1.0, e.g. `0.85` for 85% opacity) on
    shape, textbox, and table cell background colors.
-   **`outline_color`**: Hex color (e.g., `"#FF0000"`) to style the shape's
    outline/border.
-   **`outline_weight`**: Line weight in points (e.g. `1.5`) for the shape's
    outline/border.
-   **`font_family`**: Set font (e.g., "Roboto", "Montserrat", "Oswald")
-   **`link`**: Add hyperlinks to text
-   **`strikethrough`**: Applies strikethrough styling to text (boolean, e.g.
    `true`)
-   **`line_spacing`**: Set line height (percentage, e.g., 150 = 1.5× spacing)
-   **`start`/`end`**: Style a range of text (not just all text) in `style-text`
-   **`content_alignment`**: Vertical text alignment inside shape/textbox.
    Allowed values: `"TOP"`, `"MIDDLE"`, `"BOTTOM"`.
-   **`line_category`**: Type of line to create (e.g. `"STRAIGHT"`, `"BENT"`,
    `"CURVED"`, defaults to `"STRAIGHT"`).
-   **`start_arrow` / `end_arrow`**: Arrowhead style (e.g. `"NONE"`,
    `"FILL_ARROW"`, `"STEALTH_ARROW"`, `"CHEVRON_ARROW"`, `"DIAMOND_ARROW"`,
    defaults to `"NONE"`).
-   **`line_weight`**: Line weight/thickness in points (e.g. `2.5`).
-   **`dash_style`**: Line dash pattern (e.g. `"SOLID"`, `"DASH"`, `"DOT"`,
    `"DASH_DOT"`, `"LONG_DASH"`, `"LONG_DASH_DOT"`).
-   **`start_connect` / `end_connect`**: Element ID of a shape to anchor each
    end of the line to, turning it into a connector that auto-routes and stays
    attached as shapes move. Accepts real element IDs (from `gslides readonly
    list-elements`) or in-batch placeholder IDs. When either is set,
    `line_category` defaults to `"BENT"`.
-   **`start_site` / `end_site`**: Connection site (edge midpoint) index on the
    connected shape: `0` = Top, `1` = Left, `2` = Bottom, `3` = Right (verified
    for `RECTANGLE`/`ROUND_RECTANGLE`). A left-to-right connector uses
    `start_site: 3`, `end_site: 1`.
-   **`updateTableColumnProperties`**: Update column widths for a table by
    passing `columnIndices` and `tableColumnProperties.columnWidth`:

    ```json
    {
      "op": "updateTableColumnProperties",
      "updateTableColumnProperties": {
        "objectId": "TABLE_1",
        "columnIndices": [0],
        "tableColumnProperties": {
          "columnWidth": {"magnitude": 65, "unit": "PT"}
        },
        "fields": "columnWidth"
      }
    }
    ```

## Slide Creation Recipe

1.  **Outline**: Decide N slides, types (title, content, stat, table, closing),
    and palette
2.  **Palette**: Pick from `references/styling.md` (Midnight Executive, Ocean
    Gradient, Cherry Bold, etc.)
3.  **Generate batch JSON**: All ops in one file, using the sandwich pattern
    (dark → light → dark)
4.  **Execute**: `gslides mutate create` then `gslides mutate batch PRES_ID -f
    batch.json`
5.  **Review**: `gslides readonly export-thumbnail` each slide, review PNG
6.  **Fix**: Second batch or individual commands
7.  **Notes**: Include `set-notes` in batch for every slide
8.  **Share**: `gslides mutate share PRES_ID --email ...`

Google Slides

Work with a Google Slides presentation the user names or links to. Everything here assumes you already have the presentation ID — the segment between /d/ and /edit in a https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/<PRESENTATION_ID>/edit URL.

Setup and Authentication

gslides auth status is the only way to tell whether you are logged in. Do not run --help, search the filesystem or environment for tokens, check another plugin's login, or run an operational command before logging in. Follow these steps exactly.

1. Register and check. Run this skill's script with auth status. It downloads the CLI, registers gslides on the agent's PATH (not the user's shell), and reports whether you are logged in:

<path/to/this/skill>/scripts/gslides auth status

# Windows (PowerShell)
& "<path\to\this\skill>\scripts\gslides.cmd" auth status

Every later call is just gslides. Never ask the user to run it; they cannot. If it reports Logged in, you are ready.

2. Log in for the user. Start this as a background command:

gslides auth login

It prints an authorization URL and exits on its own once the user approves. Read the URL from the task's log, open it in the user's browser or hand them the link, then stop and wait. Confirm with gslides auth status.

Usage

Do every Google Slides operation — reading, creating, editing, exporting, extracting images — through gslides. Run gslides --help to discover the available commands and their flags.

Two rules the CLI's own help will not tell you:

  • Never delete a slide the user did not ask you to delete. A removed slide takes its speaker notes and layout with it, and the user cannot get them back.
  • Edit the elements you were asked about, not the whole deck. Rebuilding a slide from scratch loses the theme, placeholder wiring, and notes that made it consistent with the rest of the presentation.

[!CAUTION]

gslides mutate delete-slide and gslides mutate delete-element permanently remove content from a presentation. Never run a destructive command unless the user explicitly asks.

Never share a presentation with a broad audience, a public link, or a whole organization. The user already has access to anything created on their behalf — let them handle sharing unless they explicitly instruct otherwise.

Recipes

Read and inspect:

gslides readonly read PRESENTATION_ID               # all slides as text (or --json for presentation AST)
gslides readonly read-all PRESENTATION_ID           # all slides as text (or --json for presentation AST)
gslides readonly info PRESENTATION_ID               # presentation metadata (or --json for full presentation AST)
gslides readonly list-slides PRESENTATION_ID        # list slides (or --json for slides array)
gslides readonly list-elements PRESENTATION_ID SLIDE_ID
gslides readonly get-page PRESENTATION_ID SLIDE_ID
gslides readonly get-notes PRESENTATION_ID SLIDE_ID
gslides readonly extract-images PRESENTATION_ID

Create and organize:

gslides mutate create --title "My Presentation"
gslides mutate copy PRESENTATION_ID "Copy Title"
gslides mutate add-slide PRESENTATION_ID
gslides mutate duplicate PRESENTATION_ID SLIDE_ID
gslides mutate delete-slide PRESENTATION_ID SLIDE_ID
gslides mutate reorder-slide PRESENTATION_ID SLIDE_ID --position 0

Add content:

gslides mutate add-textbox PRESENTATION_ID --slide SLIDE_ID --text "Hello" --x 100 --y 100 --width 300 --height 50 --content-alignment MIDDLE
gslides mutate add-text PRESENTATION_ID "More text" --textbox ELEMENT_ID
gslides mutate update-text PRESENTATION_ID --element ELEMENT_ID --text "New text"
gslides mutate add-image PRESENTATION_ID --slide SLIDE_ID --url "https://..." --x 100 --y 200 --width 200 --height 150
gslides mutate insert-image-from-file PRESENTATION_ID --slide SLIDE_ID --file /path/to/image.png
gslides mutate add-table PRESENTATION_ID --slide SLIDE_ID --rows 3 --cols 4
gslides mutate set-table-cell PRESENTATION_ID --table TABLE_ID --row 0 --col 0 --text "Header"
gslides mutate delete-element PRESENTATION_ID ELEMENT_ID
gslides mutate move-element PRESENTATION_ID ELEMENT_ID --x 200 --y 150
gslides mutate resize-element PRESENTATION_ID ELEMENT_ID --width 400 --height 300
gslides mutate update-shape PRESENTATION_ID --element ELEMENT_ID --text "New text" --background-color "#FF0000" --bold

Styling and export:

gslides mutate set-background PRESENTATION_ID --slide SLIDE_ID --color "#4285F4"
gslides mutate set-notes PRESENTATION_ID --slide SLIDE_ID --text "Speaker notes here"
gslides readonly export PRESENTATION_ID /tmp/pres.pdf --format pdf
gslides readonly export-thumbnail PRESENTATION_ID /tmp/slide.png
gslides mutate share PRESENTATION_ID --email user@example.com --role writer
gslides mutate batch PRESENTATION_ID requests.json

Commands

Command Description
gslides readonly read Read slide content
gslides readonly read-all Read all slides as text
gslides readonly info Presentation info
gslides mutate create Create presentation
gslides mutate copy Copy presentation
gslides readonly list-slides List slides
gslides mutate add-slide Add slide
gslides mutate duplicate Duplicate slide
gslides mutate delete-slide Delete slide
gslides mutate reorder-slide Reorder slide
gslides mutate add-textbox Add text box
gslides mutate add-text Add text to element
gslides mutate update-text Update text
gslides mutate delete-element Delete element
gslides mutate add-image Add image by URL
gslides mutate insert-image-from-file Insert local image
gslides mutate add-table Add table
gslides mutate set-table-cell Set table cell text
gslides mutate set-background Set background color
gslides mutate set-notes Set speaker notes
gslides readonly get-notes Get speaker notes
gslides mutate move-element Move element
gslides mutate resize-element Resize element
gslides mutate update-shape Update shape properties and text
gslides readonly export Export to PDF/PPTX
gslides readonly export-thumbnail Export slide as image
gslides mutate share Share presentation
gslides readonly list-elements List elements on slide
gslides readonly get-page Get page details
gslides readonly extract-images Extract all images
gslides mutate batch Execute raw batchUpdate

Tips

  • CRITICAL: Never attempt to scrape Google Slides URLs (e.g., docs.google.com/presentation/...) using web reading tools. Always use the GSlides CLI commands (gslides readonly read, gslides readonly read-all) to access presentation contents, as the URLs require authentication and will return permission errors.

  • gslides mutate set-table-cell and gslides mutate set-notes safely handle empty content (no need to pre-populate)

  • Use gslides readonly list-elements PRES_ID SLIDE_INDEX to discover element IDs for tables, textboxes, etc. The SLIDE_INDEX is 0-based (0=first slide, 1=second, etc.)

  • Reordering slides index shift: When using gslides mutate reorder-slide, the --position (which maps to InsertionIndex in Slides API) is evaluated before the source slide is removed.

    • If moving a slide to a later position (source < target): specify position = target + 1 to make it end up at index target. (e.g., to move Slide 4 (index 3) to end up at index 15, use --position 16).
    • If moving a slide to an earlier position (source > target): specify position = target to make it end up at index target.

  • The gslides mutate batch command reads a JSON file of operations for efficient bulk updates. Use --file - to pipe from stdin.

  • Removing Default Slide Elements: Newly created presentations (via gslides mutate create) contain a single title slide p with default placeholders (centered title i0 and subtitle i1). To start with a completely blank first slide, delete them at the beginning of your batch JSON file:

    [
  {"op": "delete-element", "element": "i0"},
  {"op": "delete-element", "element": "i1"}
]

  • Recommended workflow: Use gslides readonly export-thumbnail PRES_ID output.png --slide SLIDE_ID to export a slide as an image, review it visually, then iterate. This is the best way to verify layout, colors, and readability before sharing. Note: --slide takes a slide object ID (e.g. p, slide_xxx), not a 0-based index. Use gslides mutate batch --json or gslides readonly list-slides --json to get slide IDs.

Placeholder IDs (Single-Batch Workflows)

Use "id" on add-slide and add-table to create placeholder IDs that subsequent ops can reference within the same batch:

[
  {"op":"add-slide","layout":"BLANK","id":"SLIDE_1"},
  {"op":"set-background","slide":"SLIDE_1","color":"#1E2761"},
  {"op":"add-table","slide":"SLIDE_1","rows":3,"cols":3,"id":"TABLE_1"},
  {"op":"set-table-cell","table":"TABLE_1","row":0,"col":0,"text":"Header"}
]

This eliminates the need for multi-pass workflows. The CLI resolves placeholders to API-generated IDs at runtime.

set-notes for newly-created slides is automatically deferred to a second API call (the CLI handles this transparently).

Batch --json Response

Use gslides mutate batch PRES_ID -f file.json --json to get created IDs. The resolved_ids map is needed for any follow-up commands (e.g. gslides readonly export-thumbnail, gslides mutate insert-image-from-file) that target created slides:

{"operations":12,"api_requests":30,"created_slides":["slide_xxx"],"created_tables":["table_xxx"],"resolved_ids":{"SLIDE_1":"slide_xxx","TABLE_1":"table_xxx"}}

Card Design Tips (from Testing)

  • Use header + body combo — two textboxes (bold 20pt header + 13-14pt body) instead of one tall card. This avoids empty space and gives visual hierarchy.
  • Accent dividers: thin rectangles (3-4px height) between card sections add polish.
  • Bottom taglines: centered muted text below cards fills vertical whitespace.
  • Stat call-outs: rounded rectangles with big numbers (36pt+) make overview slides more visual.

Batch Operations Reference

The batch command supports 27 operations:

Op Key Fields Description
set-background slide, color Slide background color
add-text element, textbox, text Insert text into element. Use this to safely insert text into empty placeholders/shapes, as update-text may fail.
add-textbox slide, text, x, y, width, height, font_size, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, color, background_color, alpha, font_family, alignment, content_alignment, line_spacing, link Create textbox with text and styling
add-image slide, url, x, y, width, height Insert image from URL
add-slide layout, id Add slide (default: BLANK). 'layout' supports standard enums or custom layout IDs (e.g. g43cb3ecfc4_0_85). Hint: Discover custom IDs by running the gslides readonly info --json command on reference deck. 'id' creates a placeholder for use by later ops
add-table slide, rows, cols, id, width, height, x, y Create table with optional size and coordinates. id creates a placeholder for set-table-cell
add-line slide, line_category, x, y, width, height, start_arrow, end_arrow, line_weight, color, dash_style, start_connect, end_connect, start_site, end_site, id Create a straight line, arrow, or shape-anchored connector. Set start_connect/end_connect to shape element IDs (with start_site/end_site edge index) to anchor and auto-route between shapes; connected lines default to BENT. id creates a placeholder for use by later ops
set-table-cell table, row, col, text, color, bold, font_size, font_family, underline, strikethrough, background_color, alpha Set + style table cell
style-text element, color, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, font_size, font_family, link, start, end Restyle existing text
style-table-cell table, row, col, color, bold, font_size, font_family, underline, strikethrough, alignment, start, end Restyle table cell text or alignment (optional range start/end)
set-notes slide, text Set speaker notes
delete-element element Delete element by ID
delete-text element, start, end Delete text range
move-element element, x, y Move element
resize-element element, width, height, x, y Resize element
update-text element, text Replace text in element
update-alt-text element, description, title Replace alt text in element
add-shape slide, shape_type, x, y, width, height, background_color, alpha Create shape (RECTANGLE, ELLIPSE, etc.)
style-shape element, background_color, alpha, outline_color, outline_weight Change shape fill color, border/outline color and weight
duplicate-slide slide, id, elements Duplicate a slide
reorder-slide slide, position Move slide to position
skip-slide slide Skip (hide) a slide from presentation mode
unskip-slide slide Unskip (unhide) a slide to make it visible
replace-all-text contains, replace_text Find-and-replace across deck
create-bullets element, start, end Add bullet points
update-shape element, text, background_color, alpha, color, font_size, bold, content_alignment Update shape properties and text
updateTableColumnProperties updateTableColumnProperties Update table column properties (e.g. column width)

Key Features

  • background_color: Sets shape fill on textboxes and shapes (card layouts, visual accents). Can be set to "transparent" to remove fill color.

  • alpha: Sets fill opacity (0.0 to 1.0, e.g. 0.85 for 85% opacity) on shape, textbox, and table cell background colors.

  • outline_color: Hex color (e.g., "#FF0000") to style the shape's outline/border.

  • outline_weight: Line weight in points (e.g. 1.5) for the shape's outline/border.

  • font_family: Set font (e.g., "Roboto", "Montserrat", "Oswald")

  • link: Add hyperlinks to text

  • strikethrough: Applies strikethrough styling to text (boolean, e.g. true)

  • line_spacing: Set line height (percentage, e.g., 150 = 1.5× spacing)

  • start/end: Style a range of text (not just all text) in style-text

  • content_alignment: Vertical text alignment inside shape/textbox. Allowed values: "TOP", "MIDDLE", "BOTTOM".

  • line_category: Type of line to create (e.g. "STRAIGHT", "BENT", "CURVED", defaults to "STRAIGHT").

  • start_arrow / end_arrow: Arrowhead style (e.g. "NONE", "FILL_ARROW", "STEALTH_ARROW", "CHEVRON_ARROW", "DIAMOND_ARROW", defaults to "NONE").

  • line_weight: Line weight/thickness in points (e.g. 2.5).

  • dash_style: Line dash pattern (e.g. "SOLID", "DASH", "DOT", "DASH_DOT", "LONG_DASH", "LONG_DASH_DOT").

  • start_connect / end_connect: Element ID of a shape to anchor each end of the line to, turning it into a connector that auto-routes and stays attached as shapes move. Accepts real element IDs (from gslides readonly list-elements) or in-batch placeholder IDs. When either is set, line_category defaults to "BENT".

  • start_site / end_site: Connection site (edge midpoint) index on the connected shape: 0 = Top, 1 = Left, 2 = Bottom, 3 = Right (verified for RECTANGLE/ROUND_RECTANGLE). A left-to-right connector uses start_site: 3, end_site: 1.

  • updateTableColumnProperties: Update column widths for a table by passing columnIndices and tableColumnProperties.columnWidth:

    {
  "op": "updateTableColumnProperties",
  "updateTableColumnProperties": {
    "objectId": "TABLE_1",
    "columnIndices": [0],
    "tableColumnProperties": {
      "columnWidth": {"magnitude": 65, "unit": "PT"}
    },
    "fields": "columnWidth"
  }
}

Slide Creation Recipe

  1. Outline: Decide N slides, types (title, content, stat, table, closing), and palette
  2. Palette: Pick from references/styling.md (Midnight Executive, Ocean Gradient, Cherry Bold, etc.)
  3. Generate batch JSON: All ops in one file, using the sandwich pattern (dark → light → dark)
  4. Execute: gslides mutate create then gslides mutate batch PRES_ID -f batch.json
  5. Review: gslides readonly export-thumbnail each slide, review PNG
  6. Fix: Second batch or individual commands
  7. Notes: Include set-notes in batch for every slide
  8. Share: gslides mutate share PRES_ID --email ...
