**`residues`** (both `highlight_region` and `annotate_region`) is a list of
residue numbers and/or `{"auth_asym_id", "start_auth_seq_id",
"end_auth_seq_id"}` objects, in any mix. A number is one residue on
`auth_asym_id`: `[6, 10]` means residues 6 and 10, not the span 6–10. Use an
object only for a span (`{"start_auth_seq_id": 57, "end_auth_seq_id": 60}`) or a
residue on another chain; `end_auth_seq_id` defaults to `start_auth_seq_id` and
a missing `auth_asym_id` defaults to the top-level `auth_asym_id`.
`start_auth_seq_id`/`end_auth_seq_id` is shorthand for a single span. Entries of
`activeSelection` (`{"startResidue", "endResidue"}`, see
[Current User Selection](#current-user-selection-stateactiveselection)) are
accepted too, as they are. Only this form carries residue names: when the user
gives them, or you read them from the structure file
(`_atom_site.auth_comp_id`), pass them as `auth_comp_id`, e.g. `{"startResidue":
{"auth_seq_id": 57, "auth_comp_id": "HIS"}, "endResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 60,
"auth_comp_id": "GLY"}}`. They are stored as given (not checked against the
structure).

**`chains`** (both tools) lists **whole chains** by `auth_asym_id`, e.g.
`chains=["B"]`. Use it whenever the user means an entire chain ("color chain B
red", "note on chain C") rather than listing the chain's residues; it can be
combined with `residues` on other chains. The viewer fills in the chain's
residues from the loaded structure and shows it as `Chain B`.

When the same note applies to several residues, make **one** `annotate_region`
call listing all of them — do not create one note per residue. Likewise, one
`highlight_region` call colors all listed residues.

**Choose by whether the request includes text, not by the verb.** Users may say
"highlight", "color", "annotate", "note", "label" or anything else:

*   The request attaches **text** to residues (a label, note, name or comment),
    even when it also asks for a color ("highlight the catalytic triad in blue
    and label it"): make **one** `annotate_region` call, passing the color as
    `color`. An annotation colors its residues itself.
*   The request asks for **color only**, even when it says what the residues are
    ("color the binding-site residues green"): call `highlight_region`. Don't
    invent a label the user did not ask for.
*   Never call both on the same residues: that adds a second, unlabelled entry,
    which the viewer lists as a separate "No annotation" card.

Calling `annotate_region` on exactly the residues of an existing note (e.g. one
the user added in the viewer) **overwrites** that note's text, keeping its `id`,
position and color unless you pass `color`. So when the user asks to add
information to a note they already made, call `annotate_region` on the same
residues with the full new text (include anything worth keeping from the old
note, returned as `previousNote`). A note on different or only partly
overlapping residues is added alongside.

### Examples

**Load a downloaded AlphaFold model:**
`load_structure(id="P00533/AF-P00533-F1-model_v6.cif")`

**Load a downloaded PDB entry:** `pdb-database`'s `download_coordinate_files.py
--ids 4HHB --format mmcif --output_dir <conv artifact dir>/4HHB` saves
`4HHB/pdb_00004hhb.cif.gz`. The viewer does not read gzipped files, so `gunzip`
it first, then `load_structure(id="4HHB/pdb_00004hhb.cif")`.

**Load from a conversation artifact:** `load_structure(id="prediction.cif",
source="artifact")`

**Rejected:** `load_structure(id="1CRN")`,
`load_structure(id="https://files.rcsb.org/download/1CRN.cif")`. Download the
file first.

**Change representation and hide waters:** `set_representation(style="stick",
components={"waters": false})`

**Show annotation pins and hide pLDDT coloring:**
`set_overlays(annotations=true, confidence=false)`

**Highlight an active site in blue:** `highlight_region(start_auth_seq_id=50,
end_auth_seq_id=60, auth_asym_id="A", color="#0000ff")`

**One note on two separate residues:** `annotate_region(text="hi 2",
auth_asym_id="A", residues=[6, 10])`

**Annotate a binding pocket:** `annotate_region(start_auth_seq_id=100,
end_auth_seq_id=115, text="ATP binding pocket", auth_asym_id="A")`

**Annotate a site spanning two chains:**

```
annotate_region(residues=[{"auth_asym_id": "A", "start_auth_seq_id": 57,
                           "end_auth_seq_id": 60},
                          {"auth_asym_id": "B", "start_auth_seq_id": 102}],
                text="Catalytic triad")
```

**Remove that note:** `remove_annotation(id="s3")` (use the `id` returned by
`annotate_region` or listed in `get_state`)

**Update or recolor a note:** call `annotate_region` again with the same
`residues`, the new `text`, and optionally the new `color`; the existing note is
overwritten in place. (The user can also rename a note from the viewer's side
panel, or recolor it by saving it again on the same residues.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Rendering Styles

The `style` parameter on `load_structure` and `set_representation` controls the
3D rendering representation:

Value     | Description
--------- | -----------------------------------------
`cartoon` | Ribbon / helix / sheet backbone (default)
`stick`   | Bond sticks with small atom spheres
`sphere`  | Van der Waals spacefill spheres
`surface` | Gaussian molecular surface
`line`    | Thin lines connecting bonded atoms

## Molecular Components

The optional `components` parameter on `set_representation` controls visibility
of specific molecular component categories. All sub-properties are boolean; a
structure shown for the first time has only `ligands` on:

Sub-property | Description
------------ | -------------------------------------
`waters`     | Solvent water molecules
`sugars`     | Carbohydrate / glycan chains
`ligands`    | Non-polymer small-molecule ligands
`sidechains` | Amino acid sidechains (Cβ and beyond)

## Overlays (`annotations` and `confidence`)

Use **`set_overlays`** to switch the two viewport overlays on or off. Pass only
the overlays you want to change:

Overlay       | Default | Description
------------- | ------- | -----------------------------------------
`annotations` | `false` | 3D annotation pins and ribbon highlights.
`confidence`  | `true`  | Per-residue pLDDT confidence 3D coloring.

```
set_overlays(annotations=true)
set_overlays(confidence=false)
```

Both flags are kept per structure (see
[Per-structure view state](#per-structure-view-state-statestructures)): a
structure shown for the first time starts from the defaults, and switching back
to one restores its flags. `annotate_region` turns `annotations` on by itself.
The viewer does not turn it on just because a structure has saved notes: call
`set_overlays(annotations=true)` when the user wants to see existing notes. The
user can also show or hide each overlay with the eye button in the header of the
**Selections** and **Confidence** sections of the viewer's side panel (opened
with the button at the top right of the viewport); don't call `set_overlays`
just to preserve their choice.

Predicted models that carry per-residue confidence scores (AlphaFold DB,
ColabFold, ESMFold, and similar) are colored by pLDDT; the side panel's
**Confidence** section shows the legend and the share of residues in each band.
Detection is based on the contents of the file, not its name, so `confidence` is
a no-op on an experimental structure — it keeps its default coloring and no
Confidence section appears.

Call `set_overlays(confidence=false)` when the user wants to see a predicted
model in the standard color scheme, for example to compare it side by side with
an experimental structure.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Per-structure view state (`state.structures`)

Each structure the viewer has shown keeps its own view state in
**`structures`**, keyed by the structure's workspace path (or artifact
filename): its `style`, `components`, `selections`, `annotations` and
`confidence`. The structure shown is the one named by the top-level `source` and
`path`/`filename`; `nextSelectionId` and the user's `activeSelection` stay at
the top level:

```json
{"source": "workspace", "path": "4HHB/4hhb.cif",
 "nextSelectionId": 4, "activeSelection": null,
 "structures": {
   "4HHB/4hhb.cif": {"style": "stick", "annotations": true,
                     "selections": {"s3": {"label": "Heme pocket", ...}}},
   "1crn.cif": {"confidence": false,
                "selections": {"s1": {"color": "#ff1f3d", ...}}}}}
```

*   Switching structures (`load_structure`, the viewer's file list or an upload)
    only changes which structure is shown; switching back restores its
    selections, style, components and overlays. A structure with no entry is
    shown with the defaults: `cartoon`, only ligands visible, `annotations` off,
    `confidence` on.
*   `set_representation`, `set_overlays` and the selection tools act on the
    structure shown only. To change another structure, load it first.
*   An entry holding nothing but defaults is removed.
*   Those tools need a structure to be shown: until one is, they return an
    error asking you to call `load_structure` first.

## Selections (`state.structures[...].selections`)

Color highlights and annotation notes share one id-keyed map, **`selections`**,
in the shown structure's entry of `structures`. Each entry is stored under its
selection id (`s<n>`):

```json
{"s3": {"label": "Catalytic triad", "color": "#06b6d4",
        "residues": [
          {"startResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 57, "auth_comp_id": "HIS",
                            "auth_asym_id": "A"},
           "endResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 60, "auth_comp_id": "GLY",
                          "auth_asym_id": "A"}},
          {"startResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 102, "auth_comp_id": "ASP",
                            "auth_asym_id": "B"},
           "endResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 102, "auth_comp_id": "ASP",
                          "auth_asym_id": "B"}}]}}
```

`residues` uses the same residue spans as `activeSelection` (see below): runs of
residues on one chain, from `startResidue` to `endResidue`. `auth_comp_id` is
the name passed to the tools (stored as given), replaced by the loaded
structure's name whenever the viewer saves the entry; residues named by neither
have none.

*   **Unlabelled** entry (`color`, no `label`): a color highlight.
*   **Labelled** entry: an annotation note over every range in `residues`. Its
    pin sits on the first range; ribbons and click-to-zoom cover all of them. A
    labelled entry always has a `color`: its ribbon, 3D pin, and notes-panel
    marker are drawn in it, and the user can change it in the viewer. When a
    note is created without one, it takes the color of the last color highlight
    covering its first residue (the first residue of its first range, after
    sorting), or `#ff4fa8` (hot pink) if that residue is not colored. Entries
    read without a `color` get one by the same rule.
*   Entries are painted in map order: where a note and a color highlight
    overlap, whichever comes later in `selections` is on top.
*   The key (`s<n>`) is the selection's stable `id` and is what
    `remove_annotation` takes. Spans are sorted by chain and start, and
    overlapping or contiguous spans are merged.
*   Ids are unique across structures and never reused, even after an entry is
    removed. The next free number is kept in the top-level `nextSelectionId`;
    don't edit it.
*   An entry the user saved with whole chains selected (every residue of the
    chain, however it was picked), or that `highlight_region`/ `annotate_region`
    wrote with `chains`, also has `"chains": ["A", ...]`: the chains selected
    whole, which the viewer lists as `Chain A` instead of their residue ranges
    (residues selected on other chains are listed one by one, in the same
    entry). `residues` lists every span of those chains too, so read the
    residues from `residues`. Right after a tool call a chain may have no spans
    in `residues` yet: the viewer fills in the chain's polymer residues from the
    loaded structure, or all of its residues for a chain with no polymer (e.g.
    only ligands), and drops chains the structure does not have. The viewer
    drops a chain from `chains` once its spans change.

## Current User Selection (`state.activeSelection`)

The residues the user has selected right now (clicked in 3D or the sequence
panel, not yet saved) are reported by the viewer as **`activeSelection`**, a
list of runs of residues on one chain, each from `startResidue` to `endResidue`
(the same residue for a single one). A residue is `{"auth_seq_id",
"auth_comp_id", "auth_asym_id"}` (the mmCIF author residue number, residue name
and chain), with `auth_comp_id` read from the loaded structure (left out when
unknown); `[]` when nothing is selected:

```json
{"activeSelection": [
  {"startResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 1, "auth_comp_id": "ADP",
                    "auth_asym_id": "A"},
   "endResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 1, "auth_comp_id": "ADP",
                  "auth_asym_id": "A"}},
  {"startResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 308, "auth_comp_id": "THR",
                    "auth_asym_id": "A"},
   "endResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 310, "auth_comp_id": "LYS",
                  "auth_asym_id": "A"}}]}
```

When the user refers to "this residue", "the selected residues", or "what I
clicked", call `get_state` and use `activeSelection`, e.g. pass its entries as
they are as `residues` to `annotate_region` or `highlight_region`. If it is
empty, ask the user which residues they mean. It is read-only and transient: the
viewer overwrites it on every selection change, so don't write it, and don't
treat it as a saved highlight or note.

> [!IMPORTANT] **Author numbering**: all ids are author ids (`auth_asym_id`,
> `auth_seq_id`, `auth_comp_id`), never `label_*`. In 2GXA, author chain A
> residue 1 is ADP; label chain A residue 1 is a DT of author chain M.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Coloring Specific Residues

Use **`highlight_region`** to color specific residues, functional sites, active
pockets, or mutation sites **without creating annotation labels**:

```
highlight_region(residues=[50, 51, 52, 53], auth_asym_id="A",
                   color="#0000ff")
highlight_region(start_auth_seq_id=100, end_auth_seq_id=110,
                   auth_asym_id="B", color="#ff0000")
highlight_region(chains=["B"], color="#ff0000")
```

Use highlights when the user only wants color, with no text. These do not create
annotation labels or notes; when the request includes text, call only
`annotate_region` (with `color`), which colors the residues too. `auth_asym_id`
is optional and defaults to `A`. To color an **entire chain**, pass `chains`
instead of guessing its residue range: the viewer fills in the chain's residues
from the loaded structure and lists it as `Chain B`.

`#ff4fa8` is reserved for annotation ribbons. Avoid it, or your highlights will
be indistinguishable from annotation markers.

`highlight_region` stacks: the new color entry is drawn on top of older entries
on the same residues, notes included, which keep their residues and color, so
deleting it (the user can, in the Selections list) shows them again. Each call
adds an entry, so don't recolor residues just to restate a color they already
have.

Users color residues themselves from the viewer's side panel. A click in 3D or
in the sequence panel selects a residue (or a whole chain, with **Select:
Chain**), Shift+click adds the range from the last clicked residue to the
clicked one and zooms to everything selected (in ball-and-stick), Ctrl /
Cmd+click adds the clicked residue or removes it and zooms to everything
selected too, and a click on empty space or Escape clears it. The **Select &
customize** section lists what is selected as chips (a residue each, or `Chain
X` for a chain whose residues are all selected, whichever mode picked them; each
with a button that removes it from the selection), plus **Clear**. Below the
chips the user picks a color (swatches of the color names above and the note
pink, or a custom color from a picker or `#rrggbb`; the first swatch is
preselected), may type an annotation, and presses the single **Save**. Save
without an annotation paints the selection; with one it saves the note on those
residues, drawn in the chosen color (see **User 3D Annotations & Context
Notes**). These colors follow the same rules as `highlight_region` and are saved
to `selections` as unlabelled entries, so the agent and the user share them:
`get_state` returns what the user painted, and `clear_highlights` removes the
user's colors too.

To clear all highlights, call **`clear_highlights`**.

Highlights are scoped to the structure they were applied to: each structure
keeps its own in its `structures` entry. Switching structures shows only the new
structure's highlights, so a range like "chain A, 50-60" never colors unrelated
residues of another structure, and switching back brings them back.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## User 3D Annotations & Context Notes

Annotation notes are the labelled entries of **`selections`**, shared by the
agent and the user. Users write notes in the side panel's **Select & customize**
section: select residues (in 3D or the sequence, across ranges and chains), pick
a color, type in the **Annotation** field and press Enter or Save. A note saved
on exactly the residues of an existing note replaces it, as with
`annotate_region`. Every entry of `selections`, notes and color highlights, is
listed in the **Selections** section below; a color highlight's card reads "No
annotation". Each card has a pencil to write the note in place (Enter or the
check saves, Escape cancels; giving a color highlight a note makes it a note), a
trash icon to delete the entry, and a chip per residue range; clicking a card, a
chip or a pin zooms to it. **Delete All** removes every entry. Notes the user
writes and notes you add with `annotate_region` end up in the same list, and
`get_state` always returns the current list. No annotation file is written to
disk.



| Task                   | Tool                                   |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Add a note             | `annotate_region(text,                 |
:                        : start_auth_seq_id, end_auth_seq_id,    :
:                        : auth_asym_id)` or                      :
:                        : `annotate_region(text, residues)`,     :
:                        : which also turns the `annotations`     :
:                        : overlay on                             :
| Read the notes         | `get_state`, then use the `selections` |
:                        : entries that have a `label`            :
| Update a note          | `annotate_region` on the same residues |
:                        : with the new `text` (and `color`)      :
| Remove one note        | `remove_annotation(id)`                |
| Remove every note      | `clear_annotations()`                  |
| Show or hide the notes | `set_overlays(annotations=true/false)` |



Notes belong to the loaded structure, and each structure keeps its own list.
`load_structure` and switching structures in the viewer show the new structure's
notes (none the first time it is shown); switching back restores the old
structure's notes.

A note added with `annotate_region` and no `color` takes the color its residues
are painted in (pink otherwise); a note saved in the viewer takes the color
chosen next to it. Saving a color without a note from the viewer's **Select &
customize** section (see **Coloring Specific Residues**) leaves notes alone: the
color is drawn on top of any note on those residues. Users change a note's color
by saving the note again on the same residues.

### Agent Instructions for Handling Annotations

When the user asks about 3D biomolecular structure annotations, highlighted
residues, structure notes, or says *"tell me about the regions I've annotated"*:

1.  **READ ACTIVE STATE**: Call `get_state`. Check which structure is displayed
    and read the `selections` of its `structures` entry (labelled entries are
    notes, unlabelled ones are color highlights).
2.  **STRICT FIDELITY RULE**: Comment ONLY on the notes and highlights returned
    by `get_state`. Do NOT guess, hallucinate, or recall residues from previous
    turns or unselected regions.
3.  **SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH**: Before each answer, call `get_state` again,
    because the user can add or delete notes in the viewer at any time.
4.  **Synthesize Structural Analysis**: Provide detailed per-residue structural
    analysis (secondary structure location, hydrophobic packing, hydrogen
    bonding, disulfide bonds, domain boundaries, and mutation impacts) strictly
    for active annotations.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Key Principles

1.  **MCP tools are the only interface**: Always use the tools in the MCP Tool
    Catalog above (`load_structure`, `set_representation`, `set_overlays`,
    `highlight_region`, `clear_highlights`, `annotate_region`,
    `remove_annotation`, `clear_annotations`, `get_state`). Never open or edit
    the viewer's own code, config or saved state: nothing in them helps operate
    the viewer.
2.  **Scope files to the current conversation**: Store downloaded structure
    files as conversation artifacts.
3.  **Check active state**: Call `get_state` to verify what the viewer is
    actively displaying before answering questions about the visualization.
4.  **Delegate data retrieval**: Use `pdb-database` or
    `alphafold-database-fetch-and-analyze` when files need to be searched,
    downloaded, or analyzed on disk.
5.  **Keep visualizations in the sidecar**: Avoid dumping heavy raw coordinate
    text or ASCII drawings into chat.
6.  **Fix failed loads**: When the viewer can't show the state, you receive the
    notification `BiomolecularStructureViewer: <message>`. Check the file and
    that `id` is its path, fix the arguments or the file (download a bad file
    again with `curl`), and call the tool again. Save a fixed file under a new
    name: the same `id` does not reload. If both are fine, tell the user the
    viewer couldn't load it and stop.
normalizedHtml:
Biomolecular Structure Viewer

The Biomolecular Structure Viewer sidecar renders interactive 3D molecular structures in the Antigravity side pane using Mol*.

All interaction with the viewer is through the science_biomolecular_structure_viewer_mcp MCP tool catalog. Never open or edit the viewer's own code, config or saved state; the MCP tools are the only way to operate it. They validate inputs, apply atomic state patches, and prevent race conditions.

[!IMPORTANT] Local files only: The viewer only loads structure files saved locally. Always download the structure into the current conversation's artifact directory first (using pdb-database or alphafold-database-fetch-and-analyze, see Where files live), then pass the file path to load_structure. Database IDs (e.g. 1CRN, P01308, AF-P01308-F1) and URLs are rejected; download URLs into the artifact directory first with curl, not a web-page fetch tool such as read_url_content, which can silently truncate large files.

Where files live

The viewer is scoped to the current conversation: it only lists and loads structure files from that conversation's artifact directory.

Viewer state (including user notes) is managed entirely by the MCP tools; never read or write it directly.

Standard Biomolecular Structure Visualization Workflow

When the user asks to visualise, show, or display a biomolecular structure:

  1. Obtain Local Structure File (Required):

    • If the structure file (.cif, .mmcif, or .pdb) is already in the conversation's artifact directory (including .user_uploaded/), use its path relative to that directory.
    • If the file is elsewhere on disk (e.g. the user's workspace), copy it into the conversation's artifact directory first (e.g. cp): the viewer does not load files from outside it.
    • If given a protein name, gene symbol, UniProt ID, or PDB ID, use appropriate search/fetch skills or tools (e.g. pdb-database, alphafold-database-fetch-and-analyze) to download the 3D coordinate file into the conversation's artifact directory. Decompress .gz files (e.g. gunzip); the viewer does not read gzipped files.
    • If the download fails, tell the user why and stop. Do not pass the database ID to load_structure: it is rejected.

  2. Load into Viewer: Call the load_structure MCP tool with the local file path relative to the conversation directory (e.g. P00533/AF-P00533-F1-model_v6.cif or 4HHB/pdb_00004hhb.cif).

  3. Surface Sidecar Link: Always include this link in your chat response so the user can open the viewer with one click:

    [Biomolecular Structure Viewer](sidecar://science/biomolecular_structure_viewer/ui.html)

MCP Tool Catalog (science_biomolecular_structure_viewer_mcp)

Tool Parameters Description
get_state (none) Returns the sidecar's current state (active structure, selections, the user's activeSelection) and state version.
load_structure id (required), source (optional: 'workspace' | 'artifact') Loads a local structure file into the viewer: a workspace/artifact file path or artifact filename. Database IDs and URLs are rejected (download first). Each structure keeps its own selections, style and overlays (see Per-structure view state): switching back restores them, and loading the structure already shown changes nothing. source is auto-detected when omitted.
set_representation style (required: 'cartoon' | 'stick' | 'sphere' | 'surface' | 'line'), components (optional: {waters, sugars, ligands, sidechains}) Changes the 3D rendering representation and optional molecular component visibility flags.
set_overlays annotations, confidence (optional booleans; pass at least one) Shows or hides the annotation pins / notes overlay and the pLDDT confidence coloring and legend. See Overlays below.
highlight_region residues (see below) or start_auth_seq_id / end_auth_seq_id; auth_asym_id (default 'A'), color (named color or #rrggbb) Appends ONE unlabelled color entry (Mol* overpaint) covering every listed residue to selections, without creating an annotation note. Returns its id. It is drawn on top of older entries, notes included, which keep their residues and color.
annotate_region text (required); residues (see below) or start_auth_seq_id / end_auth_seq_id; auth_asym_id (default 'A'); color (optional; defaults to the residue's color, else #ff4fa8) Appends ONE labelled entry (annotation note) covering every listed residue, possibly on several chains, to selections and turns the annotations overlay on. Returns its id and the resolved color. If a note already covers exactly these residues, it is updated in place instead (updated is true; same id).
remove_annotation id (required, e.g. 's2') Removes the annotation note with that id. Errors (listing valid ids) if it is not a labelled entry.
clear_annotations (none) Removes all labelled entries (notes). Color highlights stay.
clear_highlights (none) Removes all unlabelled entries (color highlights). Notes stay.

residues (both highlight_region and annotate_region) is a list of residue numbers and/or {"auth_asym_id", "start_auth_seq_id", "end_auth_seq_id"} objects, in any mix. A number is one residue on auth_asym_id: [6, 10] means residues 6 and 10, not the span 6–10. Use an object only for a span ({"start_auth_seq_id": 57, "end_auth_seq_id": 60}) or a residue on another chain; end_auth_seq_id defaults to start_auth_seq_id and a missing auth_asym_id defaults to the top-level auth_asym_id. start_auth_seq_id/end_auth_seq_id is shorthand for a single span. Entries of activeSelection ({"startResidue", "endResidue"}, see Current User Selection) are accepted too, as they are. Only this form carries residue names: when the user gives them, or you read them from the structure file (_atom_site.auth_comp_id), pass them as auth_comp_id, e.g. {"startResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 57, "auth_comp_id": "HIS"}, "endResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 60, "auth_comp_id": "GLY"}}. They are stored as given (not checked against the structure).

chains (both tools) lists whole chains by auth_asym_id, e.g. chains=["B"]. Use it whenever the user means an entire chain ("color chain B red", "note on chain C") rather than listing the chain's residues; it can be combined with residues on other chains. The viewer fills in the chain's residues from the loaded structure and shows it as Chain B.

When the same note applies to several residues, make one annotate_region call listing all of them — do not create one note per residue. Likewise, one highlight_region call colors all listed residues.

Choose by whether the request includes text, not by the verb. Users may say "highlight", "color", "annotate", "note", "label" or anything else:

  • The request attaches text to residues (a label, note, name or comment), even when it also asks for a color ("highlight the catalytic triad in blue and label it"): make one annotate_region call, passing the color as color. An annotation colors its residues itself.
  • The request asks for color only, even when it says what the residues are ("color the binding-site residues green"): call highlight_region. Don't invent a label the user did not ask for.
  • Never call both on the same residues: that adds a second, unlabelled entry, which the viewer lists as a separate "No annotation" card.

Calling annotate_region on exactly the residues of an existing note (e.g. one the user added in the viewer) overwrites that note's text, keeping its id, position and color unless you pass color. So when the user asks to add information to a note they already made, call annotate_region on the same residues with the full new text (include anything worth keeping from the old note, returned as previousNote). A note on different or only partly overlapping residues is added alongside.

Examples

Load a downloaded AlphaFold model: load_structure(id="P00533/AF-P00533-F1-model_v6.cif")

Load a downloaded PDB entry: pdb-database's download_coordinate_files.py --ids 4HHB --format mmcif --output_dir <conv artifact dir>/4HHB saves 4HHB/pdb_00004hhb.cif.gz. The viewer does not read gzipped files, so gunzip it first, then load_structure(id="4HHB/pdb_00004hhb.cif").

Load from a conversation artifact: load_structure(id="prediction.cif", source="artifact")

Rejected: load_structure(id="1CRN"), load_structure(id="https://files.rcsb.org/download/1CRN.cif"). Download the file first.

Change representation and hide waters: set_representation(style="stick", components={"waters": false})

Show annotation pins and hide pLDDT coloring: set_overlays(annotations=true, confidence=false)

Highlight an active site in blue: highlight_region(start_auth_seq_id=50, end_auth_seq_id=60, auth_asym_id="A", color="#0000ff")

One note on two separate residues: annotate_region(text="hi 2", auth_asym_id="A", residues=[6, 10])

Annotate a binding pocket: annotate_region(start_auth_seq_id=100, end_auth_seq_id=115, text="ATP binding pocket", auth_asym_id="A")

Annotate a site spanning two chains:

annotate_region(residues=[{"auth_asym_id": "A", "start_auth_seq_id": 57,
                           "end_auth_seq_id": 60},
                          {"auth_asym_id": "B", "start_auth_seq_id": 102}],
                text="Catalytic triad")

Remove that note: remove_annotation(id="s3") (use the id returned by annotate_region or listed in get_state)

Update or recolor a note: call annotate_region again with the same residues, the new text, and optionally the new color; the existing note is overwritten in place. (The user can also rename a note from the viewer's side panel, or recolor it by saving it again on the same residues.)

Rendering Styles

The style parameter on load_structure and set_representation controls the 3D rendering representation:

Value Description
cartoon Ribbon / helix / sheet backbone (default)
stick Bond sticks with small atom spheres
sphere Van der Waals spacefill spheres
surface Gaussian molecular surface
line Thin lines connecting bonded atoms

Molecular Components

The optional components parameter on set_representation controls visibility of specific molecular component categories. All sub-properties are boolean; a structure shown for the first time has only ligands on:

Sub-property Description
waters Solvent water molecules
sugars Carbohydrate / glycan chains
ligands Non-polymer small-molecule ligands
sidechains Amino acid sidechains (Cβ and beyond)

Overlays (annotations and confidence)

Use set_overlays to switch the two viewport overlays on or off. Pass only the overlays you want to change:

Overlay Default Description
annotations false 3D annotation pins and ribbon highlights.
confidence true Per-residue pLDDT confidence 3D coloring. 
set_overlays(annotations=true)
set_overlays(confidence=false)

Both flags are kept per structure (see Per-structure view state): a structure shown for the first time starts from the defaults, and switching back to one restores its flags. annotate_region turns annotations on by itself. The viewer does not turn it on just because a structure has saved notes: call set_overlays(annotations=true) when the user wants to see existing notes. The user can also show or hide each overlay with the eye button in the header of the Selections and Confidence sections of the viewer's side panel (opened with the button at the top right of the viewport); don't call set_overlays just to preserve their choice.

Predicted models that carry per-residue confidence scores (AlphaFold DB, ColabFold, ESMFold, and similar) are colored by pLDDT; the side panel's Confidence section shows the legend and the share of residues in each band. Detection is based on the contents of the file, not its name, so confidence is a no-op on an experimental structure — it keeps its default coloring and no Confidence section appears.

Call set_overlays(confidence=false) when the user wants to see a predicted model in the standard color scheme, for example to compare it side by side with an experimental structure.

Per-structure view state (state.structures)

Each structure the viewer has shown keeps its own view state in structures, keyed by the structure's workspace path (or artifact filename): its style, components, selections, annotations and confidence. The structure shown is the one named by the top-level source and path/filename; nextSelectionId and the user's activeSelection stay at the top level:

{"source": "workspace", "path": "4HHB/4hhb.cif",
 "nextSelectionId": 4, "activeSelection": null,
 "structures": {
   "4HHB/4hhb.cif": {"style": "stick", "annotations": true,
                     "selections": {"s3": {"label": "Heme pocket", ...}}},
   "1crn.cif": {"confidence": false,
                "selections": {"s1": {"color": "#ff1f3d", ...}}}}}
  • Switching structures (load_structure, the viewer's file list or an upload) only changes which structure is shown; switching back restores its selections, style, components and overlays. A structure with no entry is shown with the defaults: cartoon, only ligands visible, annotations off, confidence on.
  • set_representation, set_overlays and the selection tools act on the structure shown only. To change another structure, load it first.
  • An entry holding nothing but defaults is removed.
  • Those tools need a structure to be shown: until one is, they return an error asking you to call load_structure first.

Selections (state.structures[...].selections)

Color highlights and annotation notes share one id-keyed map, selections, in the shown structure's entry of structures. Each entry is stored under its selection id (s<n>):

{"s3": {"label": "Catalytic triad", "color": "#06b6d4",
        "residues": [
          {"startResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 57, "auth_comp_id": "HIS",
                            "auth_asym_id": "A"},
           "endResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 60, "auth_comp_id": "GLY",
                          "auth_asym_id": "A"}},
          {"startResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 102, "auth_comp_id": "ASP",
                            "auth_asym_id": "B"},
           "endResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 102, "auth_comp_id": "ASP",
                          "auth_asym_id": "B"}}]}}

  • Unlabelled entry (color, no label): a color highlight.
  • Labelled entry: an annotation note over every range in residues. Its pin sits on the first range; ribbons and click-to-zoom cover all of them. A labelled entry always has a color: its ribbon, 3D pin, and notes-panel marker are drawn in it, and the user can change it in the viewer. When a note is created without one, it takes the color of the last color highlight covering its first residue (the first residue of its first range, after sorting), or #ff4fa8 (hot pink) if that residue is not colored. Entries read without a color get one by the same rule.

  • The key (s<n>) is the selection's stable id and is what remove_annotation takes. Spans are sorted by chain and start, and overlapping or contiguous spans are merged.
  • Ids are unique across structures and never reused, even after an entry is removed. The next free number is kept in the top-level nextSelectionId; don't edit it.
  • An entry the user saved with whole chains selected (every residue of the chain, however it was picked), or that highlight_region/ annotate_region wrote with chains, also has "chains": ["A", ...]: the chains selected whole, which the viewer lists as Chain A instead of their residue ranges (residues selected on other chains are listed one by one, in the same entry). residues lists every span of those chains too, so read the residues from residues. Right after a tool call a chain may have no spans in residues yet: the viewer fills in the chain's polymer residues from the loaded structure, or all of its residues for a chain with no polymer (e.g. only ligands), and drops chains the structure does not have. The viewer drops a chain from chains once its spans change.

Current User Selection (state.activeSelection)

The residues the user has selected right now (clicked in 3D or the sequence panel, not yet saved) are reported by the viewer as activeSelection, a list of runs of residues on one chain, each from startResidue to endResidue (the same residue for a single one). A residue is {"auth_seq_id", "auth_comp_id", "auth_asym_id"} (the mmCIF author residue number, residue name and chain), with auth_comp_id read from the loaded structure (left out when unknown); [] when nothing is selected:

{"activeSelection": [
  {"startResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 1, "auth_comp_id": "ADP",
                    "auth_asym_id": "A"},
   "endResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 1, "auth_comp_id": "ADP",
                  "auth_asym_id": "A"}},
  {"startResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 308, "auth_comp_id": "THR",
                    "auth_asym_id": "A"},
   "endResidue": {"auth_seq_id": 310, "auth_comp_id": "LYS",
                  "auth_asym_id": "A"}}]}

When the user refers to "this residue", "the selected residues", or "what I clicked", call get_state and use activeSelection, e.g. pass its entries as they are as residues to annotate_region or highlight_region. If it is empty, ask the user which residues they mean. It is read-only and transient: the viewer overwrites it on every selection change, so don't write it, and don't treat it as a saved highlight or note.

[!IMPORTANT] Author numbering: all ids are author ids (auth_asym_id, auth_seq_id, auth_comp_id), never label_*. In 2GXA, author chain A residue 1 is ADP; label chain A residue 1 is a DT of author chain M.

Coloring Specific Residues

Use highlight_region to color specific residues, functional sites, active pockets, or mutation sites without creating annotation labels:

highlight_region(residues=[50, 51, 52, 53], auth_asym_id="A",
                   color="#0000ff")
highlight_region(start_auth_seq_id=100, end_auth_seq_id=110,
                   auth_asym_id="B", color="#ff0000")
highlight_region(chains=["B"], color="#ff0000")

Use highlights when the user only wants color, with no text. These do not create annotation labels or notes; when the request includes text, call only annotate_region (with color), which colors the residues too. auth_asym_id is optional and defaults to A. To color an entire chain, pass chains instead of guessing its residue range: the viewer fills in the chain's residues from the loaded structure and lists it as Chain B.

#ff4fa8 is reserved for annotation ribbons. Avoid it, or your highlights will be indistinguishable from annotation markers.

highlight_region stacks: the new color entry is drawn on top of older entries on the same residues, notes included, which keep their residues and color, so deleting it (the user can, in the Selections list) shows them again. Each call adds an entry, so don't recolor residues just to restate a color they already have.

Users color residues themselves from the viewer's side panel. A click in 3D or in the sequence panel selects a residue (or a whole chain, with Select: Chain), Shift+click adds the range from the last clicked residue to the clicked one and zooms to everything selected (in ball-and-stick), Ctrl / Cmd+click adds the clicked residue or removes it and zooms to everything selected too, and a click on empty space or Escape clears it. The Select & customize section lists what is selected as chips (a residue each, or Chain X for a chain whose residues are all selected, whichever mode picked them; each with a button that removes it from the selection), plus Clear. Below the chips the user picks a color (swatches of the color names above and the note pink, or a custom color from a picker or #rrggbb; the first swatch is preselected), may type an annotation, and presses the single Save. Save without an annotation paints the selection; with one it saves the note on those residues, drawn in the chosen color (see User 3D Annotations & Context Notes). These colors follow the same rules as highlight_region and are saved to selections as unlabelled entries, so the agent and the user share them: get_state returns what the user painted, and clear_highlights removes the user's colors too.

To clear all highlights, call clear_highlights.

Highlights are scoped to the structure they were applied to: each structure keeps its own in its structures entry. Switching structures shows only the new structure's highlights, so a range like "chain A, 50-60" never colors unrelated residues of another structure, and switching back brings them back.

User 3D Annotations & Context Notes

Annotation notes are the labelled entries of selections, shared by the agent and the user. Users write notes in the side panel's Select & customize section: select residues (in 3D or the sequence, across ranges and chains), pick a color, type in the Annotation field and press Enter or Save. A note saved on exactly the residues of an existing note replaces it, as with annotate_region. Every entry of selections, notes and color highlights, is listed in the Selections section below; a color highlight's card reads "No annotation". Each card has a pencil to write the note in place (Enter or the check saves, Escape cancels; giving a color highlight a note makes it a note), a trash icon to delete the entry, and a chip per residue range; clicking a card, a chip or a pin zooms to it. Delete All removes every entry. Notes the user writes and notes you add with annotate_region end up in the same list, and get_state always returns the current list. No annotation file is written to disk.

Task Tool
Add a note annotate_region(text, start_auth_seq_id, end_auth_seq_id, auth_asym_id) or annotate_region(text, residues), which also turns the annotations overlay on
Read the notes get_state, then use the selections entries that have a label
Update a note annotate_region on the same residues with the new text (and color)
Remove one note remove_annotation(id)
Remove every note clear_annotations()
Show or hide the notes set_overlays(annotations=true/false)

Notes belong to the loaded structure, and each structure keeps its own list. load_structure and switching structures in the viewer show the new structure's notes (none the first time it is shown); switching back restores the old structure's notes.

A note added with annotate_region and no color takes the color its residues are painted in (pink otherwise); a note saved in the viewer takes the color chosen next to it. Saving a color without a note from the viewer's Select & customize section (see Coloring Specific Residues) leaves notes alone: the color is drawn on top of any note on those residues. Users change a note's color by saving the note again on the same residues.

Agent Instructions for Handling Annotations

When the user asks about 3D biomolecular structure annotations, highlighted residues, structure notes, or says "tell me about the regions I've annotated":

  1. READ ACTIVE STATE: Call get_state. Check which structure is displayed and read the selections of its structures entry (labelled entries are notes, unlabelled ones are color highlights).
  2. STRICT FIDELITY RULE: Comment ONLY on the notes and highlights returned by get_state. Do NOT guess, hallucinate, or recall residues from previous turns or unselected regions.
  3. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH: Before each answer, call get_state again, because the user can add or delete notes in the viewer at any time.
  4. Synthesize Structural Analysis: Provide detailed per-residue structural analysis (secondary structure location, hydrophobic packing, hydrogen bonding, disulfide bonds, domain boundaries, and mutation impacts) strictly for active annotations.

Key Principles

  1. MCP tools are the only interface: Always use the tools in the MCP Tool Catalog above (load_structure, set_representation, set_overlays, highlight_region, clear_highlights, annotate_region, remove_annotation, clear_annotations, get_state). Never open or edit the viewer's own code, config or saved state: nothing in them helps operate the viewer.
  2. Scope files to the current conversation: Store downloaded structure files as conversation artifacts.
  3. Check active state: Call get_state to verify what the viewer is actively displaying before answering questions about the visualization.
  4. Delegate data retrieval: Use pdb-database or alphafold-database-fetch-and-analyze when files need to be searched, downloaded, or analyzed on disk.
  5. Keep visualizations in the sidecar: Avoid dumping heavy raw coordinate text or ASCII drawings into chat.
  6. Fix failed loads: When the viewer can't show the state, you receive the notification BiomolecularStructureViewer: <message>. Check the file and that id is its path, fix the arguments or the file (download a bad file again with curl), and call the tool again. Save a fixed file under a new name: the same id does not reload. If both are fine, tell the user the viewer couldn't load it and stop.

ChEMBL Database Query

Prerequisites

  1. uv: Read the uv skill and follow its Setup instructions to ensure uv is installed and on PATH.
  2. User Notification: If .licenses/chembl_database_LICENSE.txt does not already exist in the workspace root directory then (1) prominently notify the user to check the terms at https://chembl.gitbook.io/chembl-interface-documentation/about, then (2) create the file recording the notification text and timestamp.

Core Rules

  • [!IMPORTANT] Use the Utility Scripts: You MUST ALWAYS use the provided utility script scripts/chembl_api.py for all ChEMBL API interactions, including checking status. NEVER use curl or custom Python requests to query the ChEMBL API directly. This ensures rate limit is enfoced and also retries on network errors.

  • Output to File (Required): The --output flag is required for every subcommand. All JSON results are written to the specified file. After running the command, read the output file with jq or your own code to extract the data. List results are typically wrapped in a JSON array keyed by the endpoint name (e.g., molecules, activities).

  • Notification: If this skill is used, ensure this is mentioned in the output.

Utility Script

All ChEMBL API queries use one script with subcommands:

uv run scripts/chembl_api.py <subcommand> --output <file> [options]

1. Check API Status

uv run scripts/chembl_api.py status --output /tmp/status.json

2. Molecule Queries

Fetch by ChEMBL ID: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --id CHEMBL25 --output /tmp/mol.json

Search by name: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --search "aspirin" --limit 3 --output /tmp/mol_search.json

Batch fetch: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --ids "CHEMBL25;CHEMBL1642" --limit 10 --output /tmp/mol_batch.json

Filter by properties: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --filter molecule_properties__mw_freebase__lte=500 --limit 5 --output /tmp/mol_filter.json

Filter by range: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --filter molecule_properties__mw_freebase__range=150,200 --limit 5 --output /tmp/mol_range.json

Download SDF structure file: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --id CHEMBL25 --dl_format sdf --output /tmp/aspirin.sdf

Tip: SDF/MOL files can be passed directly to tools like PyMOL or RDKit for 3D visualization and analysis.

3. Target Queries

Search for targets: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py target --search "EGFR" --limit 5 --output /tmp/targets.json

Fetch by ID: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py target --id CHEMBL203 --output /tmp/egfr.json

4. Bioactivity Data

Fetch activity by ID: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py activity --id 31863 --output /tmp/act.json

Search activities: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py activity --search "EGFR" --limit 5 --output /tmp/act_search.json

Filter activities for a target: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py activity --filter target_chembl_id=CHEMBL203 standard_type=IC50 --limit 10 --output /tmp/egfr_ic50.json

Normalize bioactivity units to nM: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py activity --filter target_chembl_id=CHEMBL203 standard_type=IC50 --limit 5 --normalize --output /tmp/egfr_normalized.json

Important: Bioactivity values come in various units (nM, µM, pM). Use --normalize to convert all values to nM for consistent comparison. Each record will include normalized_value_nM and normalization_note.

5. Drug Information

Fetch drug details: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py drug --id CHEMBL25 --output /tmp/drug.json

Drug indications: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py drug_indication --filter molecule_chembl_id=CHEMBL25 --limit 10 --output /tmp/indications.json

Filter indications by phase: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py drug_indication --filter molecule_chembl_id=CHEMBL25 max_phase_for_ind=4.0 --limit 10 --output /tmp/approved_indications.json

Drug warnings: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py drug_warning --limit 5 --output /tmp/warnings.json

Mechanisms of action: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py mechanism --filter molecule_chembl_id=CHEMBL25 --limit 5 --output /tmp/mech.json

6. Structure-Based Searches

Note: Both similarity and substructure searches are performed server-side on ChEMBL's pre-indexed database. They do not require a local RDKit installation.

Similarity search (SMILES + threshold): bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py similarity --smiles "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O" --similarity 85 --limit 5 --output /tmp/similar.json

Substructure search (SMILES): bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py substructure --smiles "c1ccccc1" --limit 5 --output /tmp/substruct.json

7. Compound Image

Download a 2D structure image (SVG by default, scalable for publication):

uv run scripts/chembl_api.py image --id CHEMBL25 --output /tmp/chembl25.svg

Options:

  • --dimensions: Image size in pixels (max 500, default 500).
  • --engine: Rendering engine (default: rdkit).
  • --img_format: Output format — svg (default, vector) or png (raster).

8. Cross-Referencing with Other Databases

ChEMBL integrates with UniProt, Ensembl, PubChem, and other databases. Common cross-referencing patterns:

Find a ChEMBL target from a UniProt accession: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py target --filter target_components__accession=P00533 --limit 5 --output /tmp/uniprot_target.json

Resolve any ChEMBL ID to its entity type: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py chembl_id_lookup --id CHEMBL203 --output /tmp/lookup.json

Look up cross-reference sources: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py xref_source --limit 10 --output /tmp/xrefs.json

Tip: Use the target_component endpoint to find UniProt accessions, gene names, and protein sequences for any ChEMBL target.

9. Pagination

All list endpoints support --limit and --offset for pagination:

# First page: 2 results starting at offset 0
uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --limit 2 --offset 0 --output /tmp/page1.json

# Second page: next 2 results starting at offset 2
uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --limit 2 --offset 2 --output /tmp/page2.json

The response includes page_meta with total_count, limit, offset, next, and previous links. Use successive --offset values to page through large result sets.

10. Other Endpoints

All remaining endpoints follow the same pattern:

uv run scripts/chembl_api.py <subcommand> --output <file> [--id ID | --ids ID1;ID2 | --search QUERY] [--limit N] [--offset N] [--filter KEY=VAL ...]

Key subcommands at a glance:

  • molecule (searchable: true): Molecules/compounds — the primary entry point
  • target (searchable: true): Drug targets (proteins, organisms, etc.)
  • activity (searchable: true): Bioactivity data (IC50, Ki, EC50, etc.)
  • drug (searchable: false): Approved drugs
  • mechanism (searchable: false): Mechanisms of action
  • assay (searchable: true): Assay descriptions
  • similarity (searchable: false): Similarity search (special)
  • substructure (searchable: false): Substructure search (special)
  • image (searchable: false): Compound image download (special)

Full subcommand list:

  • activity_supp (searchable: false): Supplementary activity data
  • assay_class (searchable: false): Assay classifications
  • atc_class (searchable: false): ATC drug classifications
  • binding_site (searchable: false): Binding site information
  • biotherapeutic (searchable: false): Biotherapeutic molecules
  • cell_line (searchable: false): Cell line details
  • chembl_id_lookup (searchable: true): ChEMBL ID resolution
  • chembl_release (searchable: false): Database release info
  • compound_record (searchable: false): Compound records
  • compound_structural_alert (searchable: false): Structural alerts
  • document (searchable: true): Literature documents
  • document_similarity (searchable: false): Document similarity
  • drug_indication (searchable: false): Drug indications
  • drug_warning (searchable: false): Drug safety warnings
  • go_slim (searchable: false): GO slim terms
  • metabolism (searchable: false): Metabolism data
  • molecule_form (searchable: false): Molecule forms (salts/parents)
  • organism (searchable: false): Organisms
  • protein_classification (searchable: true): Protein classifications
  • source (searchable: false): Data sources
  • target_component (searchable: false): Target protein components
  • target_relation (searchable: false): Target relationships
  • tissue (searchable: false): Tissue types
  • xref_source (searchable: false): Cross-reference sources
  • status (searchable: false): API status check (special)

Common Options

  • --output FILE: Required. Output file path for JSON results.
  • --id ID: Fetch a single record by ID.
  • --ids ID1;ID2;...: Batch fetch multiple records.
  • --search QUERY: Free-text search (only for searchable endpoints, marked ✓).
  • --limit N: Max results to return (default: 5).
  • --offset N: Pagination offset.
  • --filter KEY=VAL: Filter parameters (can specify multiple).
  • --normalize: (activity only) Normalize values to nM.
  • --dl_format sdf|mol: (molecule only) Download structure file.

Reference

  • API Endpoints Reference: See references/api_endpoints.md for the full list of endpoints and filter operators.

Workflow

  1. Use status --output /tmp/status.json to verify the API is available.
  2. Search for targets, molecules, or drugs using the relevant subcommand.
  3. Read the output JSON file to extract IDs and data.
  4. Use IDs from search results to fetch detailed records.
  5. Query activity with filters to get bioactivity data for targets/molecules. Use --normalize when comparing values across studies.
  6. Use similarity or substructure for server-side structure-based queries.
  7. Download compound images with image or structure files with molecule --dl_format sdf.
  8. Use target --filter target_components__accession=<UniProt> to cross- reference with UniProt.

ChEMBL Database Query

Prerequisites

  1. uv: Read the uv skill and follow its Setup instructions to ensure uv is installed and on PATH.
  2. User Notification: If .licenses/chembl_database_LICENSE.txt does not already exist in the workspace root directory then (1) prominently notify the user to check the terms at https://chembl.gitbook.io/chembl-interface-documentation/about, then (2) create the file recording the notification text and timestamp.

Core Rules

  • [!IMPORTANT] Use the Utility Scripts: You MUST ALWAYS use the provided utility script scripts/chembl_api.py for all ChEMBL API interactions, including checking status. NEVER use curl or custom Python requests to query the ChEMBL API directly. This ensures rate limit is enfoced and also retries on network errors.

  • Output to File (Required): The --output flag is required for every subcommand. All JSON results are written to the specified file. After running the command, read the output file with jq or your own code to extract the data. List results are typically wrapped in a JSON array keyed by the endpoint name (e.g., molecules, activities).

  • Notification: If this skill is used, ensure this is mentioned in the output.

Utility Script

All ChEMBL API queries use one script with subcommands:

uv run scripts/chembl_api.py <subcommand> --output <file> [options]

1. Check API Status

uv run scripts/chembl_api.py status --output /tmp/status.json

2. Molecule Queries

Fetch by ChEMBL ID: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --id CHEMBL25 --output /tmp/mol.json

Search by name: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --search "aspirin" --limit 3 --output /tmp/mol_search.json

Batch fetch: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --ids "CHEMBL25;CHEMBL1642" --limit 10 --output /tmp/mol_batch.json

Filter by properties: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --filter molecule_properties__mw_freebase__lte=500 --limit 5 --output /tmp/mol_filter.json

Filter by range: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --filter molecule_properties__mw_freebase__range=150,200 --limit 5 --output /tmp/mol_range.json

Download SDF structure file: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --id CHEMBL25 --dl_format sdf --output /tmp/aspirin.sdf

Tip: SDF/MOL files can be passed directly to tools like PyMOL or RDKit for 3D visualization and analysis.

3. Target Queries

Search for targets: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py target --search "EGFR" --limit 5 --output /tmp/targets.json

Fetch by ID: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py target --id CHEMBL203 --output /tmp/egfr.json

4. Bioactivity Data

Fetch activity by ID: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py activity --id 31863 --output /tmp/act.json

Search activities: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py activity --search "EGFR" --limit 5 --output /tmp/act_search.json

Filter activities for a target: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py activity --filter target_chembl_id=CHEMBL203 standard_type=IC50 --limit 10 --output /tmp/egfr_ic50.json

Normalize bioactivity units to nM: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py activity --filter target_chembl_id=CHEMBL203 standard_type=IC50 --limit 5 --normalize --output /tmp/egfr_normalized.json

Important: Bioactivity values come in various units (nM, µM, pM). Use --normalize to convert all values to nM for consistent comparison. Each record will include normalized_value_nM and normalization_note.

5. Drug Information

Fetch drug details: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py drug --id CHEMBL25 --output /tmp/drug.json

Drug indications: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py drug_indication --filter molecule_chembl_id=CHEMBL25 --limit 10 --output /tmp/indications.json

Filter indications by phase: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py drug_indication --filter molecule_chembl_id=CHEMBL25 max_phase_for_ind=4.0 --limit 10 --output /tmp/approved_indications.json

Drug warnings: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py drug_warning --limit 5 --output /tmp/warnings.json

Mechanisms of action: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py mechanism --filter molecule_chembl_id=CHEMBL25 --limit 5 --output /tmp/mech.json

6. Structure-Based Searches

Note: Both similarity and substructure searches are performed server-side on ChEMBL's pre-indexed database. They do not require a local RDKit installation.

Similarity search (SMILES + threshold): bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py similarity --smiles "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O" --similarity 85 --limit 5 --output /tmp/similar.json

Substructure search (SMILES): bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py substructure --smiles "c1ccccc1" --limit 5 --output /tmp/substruct.json

7. Compound Image

Download a 2D structure image (SVG by default, scalable for publication):

uv run scripts/chembl_api.py image --id CHEMBL25 --output /tmp/chembl25.svg

Options:

  • --dimensions: Image size in pixels (max 500, default 500).
  • --engine: Rendering engine (default: rdkit).
  • --img_format: Output format — svg (default, vector) or png (raster).

8. Cross-Referencing with Other Databases

ChEMBL integrates with UniProt, Ensembl, PubChem, and other databases. Common cross-referencing patterns:

Find a ChEMBL target from a UniProt accession: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py target --filter target_components__accession=P00533 --limit 5 --output /tmp/uniprot_target.json

Resolve any ChEMBL ID to its entity type: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py chembl_id_lookup --id CHEMBL203 --output /tmp/lookup.json

Look up cross-reference sources: bash uv run scripts/chembl_api.py xref_source --limit 10 --output /tmp/xrefs.json

Tip: Use the target_component endpoint to find UniProt accessions, gene names, and protein sequences for any ChEMBL target.

9. Pagination

All list endpoints support --limit and --offset for pagination:

# First page: 2 results starting at offset 0
uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --limit 2 --offset 0 --output /tmp/page1.json

# Second page: next 2 results starting at offset 2
uv run scripts/chembl_api.py molecule --limit 2 --offset 2 --output /tmp/page2.json

The response includes page_meta with total_count, limit, offset, next, and previous links. Use successive --offset values to page through large result sets.

10. Other Endpoints

All remaining endpoints follow the same pattern:

uv run scripts/chembl_api.py <subcommand> --output <file> [--id ID | --ids ID1;ID2 | --search QUERY] [--limit N] [--offset N] [--filter KEY=VAL ...]

Key subcommands at a glance:

  • molecule (searchable: true): Molecules/compounds — the primary entry point
  • target (searchable: true): Drug targets (proteins, organisms, etc.)
  • activity (searchable: true): Bioactivity data (IC50, Ki, EC50, etc.)
  • drug (searchable: false): Approved drugs
  • mechanism (searchable: false): Mechanisms of action
  • assay (searchable: true): Assay descriptions
  • similarity (searchable: false): Similarity search (special)
  • substructure (searchable: false): Substructure search (special)
  • image (searchable: false): Compound image download (special)

Full subcommand list:

  • activity_supp (searchable: false): Supplementary activity data
  • assay_class (searchable: false): Assay classifications
  • atc_class (searchable: false): ATC drug classifications
  • binding_site (searchable: false): Binding site information
  • biotherapeutic (searchable: false): Biotherapeutic molecules
  • cell_line (searchable: false): Cell line details
  • chembl_id_lookup (searchable: true): ChEMBL ID resolution
  • chembl_release (searchable: false): Database release info
  • compound_record (searchable: false): Compound records
  • compound_structural_alert (searchable: false): Structural alerts
  • document (searchable: true): Literature documents
  • document_similarity (searchable: false): Document similarity
  • drug_indication (searchable: false): Drug indications
  • drug_warning (searchable: false): Drug safety warnings
  • go_slim (searchable: false): GO slim terms
  • metabolism (searchable: false): Metabolism data
  • molecule_form (searchable: false): Molecule forms (salts/parents)
  • organism (searchable: false): Organisms
  • protein_classification (searchable: true): Protein classifications
  • source (searchable: false): Data sources
  • target_component (searchable: false): Target protein components
  • target_relation (searchable: false): Target relationships
  • tissue (searchable: false): Tissue types
  • xref_source (searchable: false): Cross-reference sources
  • status (searchable: false): API status check (special)

Common Options

  • --output FILE: Required. Output file path for JSON results.
  • --id ID: Fetch a single record by ID.
  • --ids ID1;ID2;...: Batch fetch multiple records.
  • --search QUERY: Free-text search (only for searchable endpoints, marked ✓).
  • --limit N: Max results to return (default: 5).
  • --offset N: Pagination offset.
  • --filter KEY=VAL: Filter parameters (can specify multiple).
  • --normalize: (activity only) Normalize values to nM.
  • --dl_format sdf|mol: (molecule only) Download structure file.

Reference

  • API Endpoints Reference: See references/api_endpoints.md for the full list of endpoints and filter operators.

Workflow

  1. Use status --output /tmp/status.json to verify the API is available.
  2. Search for targets, molecules, or drugs using the relevant subcommand.
  3. Read the output JSON file to extract IDs and data.
  4. Use IDs from search results to fetch detailed records.
  5. Query activity with filters to get bioactivity data for targets/molecules. Use --normalize when comparing values across studies.
  6. Use similarity or substructure for server-side structure-based queries.
  7. Download compound images with image or structure files with molecule --dl_format sdf.
  8. Use target --filter target_components__accession=<UniProt> to cross- reference with UniProt.

Clinical Trials Database

Prerequisites

  1. uv: Read the uv skill and follow its Setup instructions to ensure uv is installed and on PATH.
  2. User Notification: If .licenses/clinical_trials_database_LICENSE.txt does not already exist in the workspace root directory then (1) prominently notify the user to check the terms at https://clinicaltrials.gov/, then (2) create the file recording the notification text and timestamp.

Overview

Access worldwide clinical trial data from ClinicalTrials.gov via the REST API v2. The CLI script at scripts/clinical_trials_api.py wraps the API with dedicated flags for common filters (phase, age group, status, intervention, sponsor, etc.) so you rarely need to construct raw queries.

Core Rules

  • Use the Wrapper: ALWAYS execute the provided helper scripts to query the database rather than accessing the database directly. The scripts automatically enforce the required rate limit gracefully.
  • Always use --fields — trial JSON records can be very large; restrict to the data points you need.
  • Use --count-total first — check result volume before fetching all records.
  • Paginate large result sets — use --limit with --page-token to iterate.
  • Trust Search Filters: Do not manually re-filter results unless explicitly asked to verify detailed eligibility.
  • Notification: If this skill is used, ensure this is mentioned in the output.

Context Efficiency Warning

Trial JSON records can be very large. Always use the --fields parameter to restrict the response to only the data points you need. After writing to file, read only the fields you need rather than the entire file.

[!TIP] Use references/studies_schema.md to identify exact field paths for --fields.

Response Layout Summary

API responses contain a list of studies (usually in a studies[] array). Each study is split into protocolSection and optional resultsSection.

[!Tip] Use the shorthand aliases below with the --fields parameter to request specific data and keep responses small.

Top-Level Fields

  • totalCount — Total studies matching query (integer)
  • studies[] — Array of study objects
  • nextPageToken — cursor string for pagination

Common Study Fields (and shorthand alias)

  • Identification
    • protocolSection.identificationModule.nctId (NCTId) — Unique trial ID
    • protocolSection.identificationModule.briefTitle (BriefTitle) — Short title
  • Status
    • protocolSection.statusModule.overallStatus (OverallStatus) — Recruitment status
  • Description
    • protocolSection.descriptionModule.briefSummary (BriefSummary) — Short description
  • Arms & Interventions
    • protocolSection.armsInterventionsModule.interventions (ArmsInterventionsModule)
  • Eligibility
    • protocolSection.eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria (EligibilityCriteria) — Inclusion/Exclusion
    • protocolSection.eligibilityModule.stdAges (StdAge) — CHILD, ADULT, etc.

Consult references/studies_schema.md for full paths (Locations, Outcomes, Results) and common --fields recipes.

Commands

Search for studies

Use for: finding trials by disease, drug, phase, status, age group, or any combination of these filters.

uv run scripts/clinical_trials_api.py search \
  --condition "<disease>" \
  --intervention "<drug_or_treatment>" \
  --status "<status>" \
  --phase "<phase>" \
  --age-group "<age_group>" \
  --study-type "<study_type>" \
  --sponsor "<sponsor_name>" \
  --has-results \
  --sort "<field>:<asc|desc>" \
  --fields "<fields>" \
  --limit <N> \
  --count-total \
  --page-token "<token>" \
  --output /tmp/search_results.json

All flags are optional and combine via AND logic.

Flag reference:

  • --condition — Disease or condition to search for (e.g. "cystic fibrosis").
  • --intervention — Drug, device, or treatment name (e.g. "pembrolizumab").
  • --status — Recruitment status filter. Values: RECRUITING, COMPLETED, NOT_YET_RECRUITING, ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, ENROLLING_BY_INVITATION, TERMINATED, SUSPENDED, WITHDRAWN.
  • --phase — Trial phase filter. Values: PHASE1, PHASE2, PHASE3, PHASE4, EARLY_PHASE1, NA.
  • --age-group — Patient age group filter. Values: CHILD (0–17), ADULT (18–64), OLDER_ADULT (65+).
  • --study-type — Type of study. Values: INTERVENTIONAL, OBSERVATIONAL, EXPANDED_ACCESS.
  • --sponsor — Lead sponsor or institution name (e.g. "National Cancer Institute").
  • --has-results — Boolean flag (no value needed). When present, filters for studies that have results available on ClinicalTrials.gov.
  • --sort — Sort order as FieldName:asc or FieldName:desc. Common fields: LastUpdatePostDate, EnrollmentCount, StudyFirstPostDate, StartDate.
  • --fields — Comma-separated list of JSON field names to include in the response. Use this to keep responses small (e.g. "NCTId,BriefTitle,OverallStatus,Phase"). See references/studies_schema.md for available field paths.
  • --limit — Maximum number of studies to return per request (1–1000, default 10).
  • --count-total — Boolean flag (no value needed). When present, the response includes a totalCount field showing the total number of matching studies across all pages.
  • --page-token — An opaque cursor string used to fetch the next page of results. Obtain this value from the nextPageToken field in a previous search response. Do not construct this string yourself; always copy it verbatim from the API response. See the Pagination section below.
  • --advanced — Raw Essie filter expression for structured queries beyond the dedicated flags (e.g. "AREA[LocationCountry]United States"). Combined with other flags via AND. See references/clinical_trials_api.md for syntax.
  • --output — (Required) File path where the JSON response is written.

Example — actively recruiting Phase 3 pediatric cystic fibrosis trials:

uv run scripts/clinical_trials_api.py search \
  --condition "cystic fibrosis" \
  --status RECRUITING \
  --phase PHASE3 \
  --age-group CHILD \
  --fields "NCTId,BriefTitle,OverallStatus,Phase" \
  --limit 10 \
  --output /tmp/cf_trials.json

Example — recruiting atezolizumab trials for esophageal cancer:

uv run scripts/clinical_trials_api.py search \
  --condition "esophageal cancer" \
  --intervention "Atezolizumab" \
  --status RECRUITING \
  --fields "NCTId,BriefTitle,Phase" \
  --limit 10 \
  --output /tmp/atezolizumab_trials.json

Retrieve a study by NCT ID

Use for: fetching full details of a specific trial when you already have the NCT identifier.

uv run scripts/clinical_trials_api.py get-study \
  <nct_id> [--fields "<fields>"] \
  --output /tmp/study.json

Returns a useful default set of fields if --fields is omitted: NCTId,BriefTitle,OverallStatus,Phase,BriefSummary, ConditionsModule,ArmsInterventionsModule,EligibilityModule

Structure of the default response:

{
  "protocolSection": {
    "identificationModule": {
      "nctId": "NCT00000000",
      "briefTitle": "Study Title"
    },
    "statusModule": {
      "overallStatus": "RECRUITING"
    },
    "descriptionModule": {
      "briefSummary": "This study is about..."
    },
    "conditionsModule": {
      "conditions": [ "Condition Name" ]
    },
    "armsInterventionsModule": {
      "interventions": [ { "type": "DRUG", "name": "Drug Name" } ]
    },
    "eligibilityModule": {
      "eligibilityCriteria": "Inclusion:\n- ...",
      "stdAges": [ "ADULT" ]
    }
  }
}

Get eligibility / inclusion criteria

Use for: pulling inclusion/exclusion rules, age ranges, and sex requirements for patient-matching tasks.

uv run scripts/clinical_trials_api.py \
  get-eligibility <nct_id> \
  --output /tmp/eligibility.json

Shortcut that returns title and the full eligibility module (inclusion/exclusion criteria, age range, sex).

Example — inclusion criteria for NCT04886804:

uv run scripts/clinical_trials_api.py \
  get-eligibility NCT04886804 \
  --output /tmp/eligibility_NCT04886804.json

Count matching studies

Use for: exploring the trial landscape — checking how many trials exist for a condition, phase, or status before fetching full records.

uv run scripts/clinical_trials_api.py count \
  --condition "<disease>" \
  [--status "<status>"] [--phase "<phase>"] ... \
  --output /tmp/count.json

Returns only the total count of clinical trials matching the search criteria without fetching study records. Accepts the same filter flags as search.

Search by location / geography

Use for: narrowing trials to a specific country, state, or city.

Use --advanced with AREA[LocationCountry] or AREA[LocationCity] to restrict results by geography:

uv run scripts/clinical_trials_api.py search \
  --condition "cystic fibrosis" \
  --status RECRUITING \
  --advanced "AREA[LocationCity]New York" \
  --fields "NCTId,BriefTitle" \
  --limit 20 \
  --output /tmp/nyc_cf_trials.json

Search by sponsor / organization

Use for: identifying a sponsor's or institution's trial portfolio.

Use --sponsor to find trials run by a specific institution or company:

uv run scripts/clinical_trials_api.py search \
  --sponsor "National Cancer Institute" \
  --fields "NCTId,BriefTitle,LeadSponsorName" \
  --limit 20 \
  --output /tmp/nci_trials.json

Combined multi-criteria search

Use for: complex queries that layer multiple filters (condition and drug and phase and geography and sponsor, etc.).

All flags combine via AND, so you can layer conditions, interventions, status, phase, geography, and sponsor in a single query:

uv run scripts/clinical_trials_api.py search \
  --condition "pancreatic cancer" \
  --intervention "immunotherapy" \
  --status RECRUITING \
  --phase PHASE3 \
  --advanced "AREA[LocationCountry]United States" \
  --fields "NCTId,BriefTitle,Phase,LeadSponsorName" \
  --limit 20 \
  --output /tmp/panc_trials.json

Raw API query (escape hatch)

Use for: uncommon endpoints or parameter combinations not covered by the dedicated flags.

uv run scripts/clinical_trials_api.py raw-query \
  --endpoint <path> \
  --params '<json_dict>' \
  --output /tmp/raw_result.json

Pagination

When results exceed --limit, the response includes a nextPageToken. Pass it with --page-token to fetch the next page:

uv run scripts/clinical_trials_api.py search \
  --condition "breast cancer" \
  --status RECRUITING \
  --limit 50 --count-total \
  --output /tmp/breast_cancer_p1.json

uv run scripts/clinical_trials_api.py search \
  --condition "breast cancer" \
  --status RECRUITING \
  --limit 50 --page-token "CAo=" \
  --output /tmp/breast_cancer_p2.json

Advanced Querying

For complex filtering beyond the dedicated flags, use --advanced with an Essie expression.

What is an Essie Expression? Essie is the search engine powering ClinicalTrials.gov. An Essie expression is a structured query that targets specific fields (e.g., country, phase) rather than doing general keyword searches.

  • AREA[Field]Value: Targets a specific field.
    • AREA[LocationCountry]United States
    • AREA[Phase]PHASE3
  • Boolean operators: Combine with AND, OR, NOT.
  • RANGE[min, max]: For numeric/date fields (e.g. RANGE[500, MAX]).

See references/clinical_trials_api.md for syntax and available fields.

It is combined with other flags via AND:

uv run scripts/clinical_trials_api.py search \
  --condition "diabetes" \
  --advanced "AREA[LocationCountry]United States \
    AND AREA[EnrollmentCount]RANGE[500, MAX]" \
  --fields "NCTId,BriefTitle,EnrollmentCount" \
  --output /tmp/diabetes_us_large.json

References

  • API parameters, enum values, and Essie syntax: references/clinical_trials_api.md
  • JSON field paths and --fields recipes: references/studies_schema.md
